So, we're at one point Alex Max like Joel, are you retiring? Like this was like a few months ago. And I had told them like, "Yes." And and so they were all all very supportive. Um there was people that know, right? Like I've been playing golf with uh Luke Whipler a little bit and he he's known for a while. I mean, most of the people have known about it, >> you know, for a while. It's actually been kept under wraps pretty good, which is which is pretty cool. >> But um I mean really everybody that has said something has just been like I appreciate it because it shows like it meant something to them, my career and and you know just being teammates with them or old coaches. Um so I appreciate everybody who's reached out and and who who said their things. But it's uh it's kind of a surreal moment. When it got announced today, my phone just started blowing up. So I don't know what I have going on right now in there. So, we'll we'll see when uh we're headed back to the house here in a little bit. >> Probably have some disappointed people around the league who are still holding out hope that maybe you're going to pull it like a week before the season. Oh, yeah. We'll go we'll go give it a go again. But you would have done that here and you made that pretty clear. Was that something you ever talked about with Joe because it feels like it was so important to you. You know, you had opportunities to to play elsewhere. Was that something that was really so important to you? And how did it become so important? Yeah, those are conversations I definitely had with Joe, with my agent, with people that have been a part of even with AB honestly. like we had talked at the end of the year and and we just, you know, I was just like, you know, this is I want to win a Super Bowl. You know, like those are the moments that you you kind of chase and and Nick Chub, you know, he went to another team and it might not, you know, you don't know what the circumstances are, but there's so many guys that have gone through it and you look across the league and like if you would have told me 10 years ago Von Miller wouldn't have been a Bronco for life or Tom Brady would have been a Patriot for life like or Aaron Rogers wouldn't have been a Packer, like those are guys that you're like, "No, these are their teams, you know?" And so for me once I got to that point I was just like this is my team. This is who I am. Like I just can't do it. And you say you want to chase a Super Bowl or you want to try and go win a Super Bowl. Like the NFL did anybody think the Seahawks were winning the Super Bowl last year? Like you know Sam it's not that easy, right? You don't just get to pick and choose which team you want to go to. And so so there was we took our time right to announce this. But that whole time I was just like there's never a chance that I'm going to go somewhere else and make this decision. Um, so it was always the Browns are nothing for me. >> I know from, you know, becoming very good friends with Joe and obviously the times that I've gotten talked to you throughout your career, like I feel like very lucky and also in some ways sad for you guys, but I have an appreciation for how you actually feel, right? >> And what you've gone through and people don't understand that like you would love to do this as long as you could. I mean, this is what you love. By the way, it's also a nice place that where you can make a heck of a lot of money and there may be not any other walks of life where you can do that right now. But take people through just like a week where because you mentioned in your thing, I can't walk on Monday. I've decided I'm going to play. Like what you actually really went through to go out there and and be there and show up for your teammates and show up for the great fans of the Cleveland Browns. >> Yeah, it the last couple years it got worse. like that that stretch where I played, you know, 6,000 snaps in a row, I was pretty healthy that stretch. Like I wasn't fighting it, but the older you get, the knees start going, the back starts going. And so last few years, there's been like two or three times a year where my back is just gone. And when it spasms, I couldn't like stand up straight. I couldn't get in and out of the car. >> Um like this year we were playing at Chicago and it was end of the year. >> It was quite cold. >> Quite cold. I got my MCL against Tennessee, like a grade two MCL, which are like one and a half, two, like they're like, you could take two weeks off if you needed to. And I was like, so on that Monday, I was like, no, I'm gonna play. Like I'm I've been in this. >> This is my last year I'm going out strong and on Tuesday, I'm rehabbing and I bent down to pick up like a kettle bell and I just like back locks up. And it's something like that, you know? So, it's not like I'm playing football and it happens. It's like I'm sneezing at a restaurant and my back locked up. >> Sneezing can be terrifying when your back is >> Yes. So I'm going through these things and then at this point it's like I can't even go in the car like cuz the car ride just like jolts you around and stuff and so I'm getting in the pool. The pool really was the only thing that helped me. So there was days where I was like Wednesday, Thursday, Friday I'm in the pool or I'm standing in meetings. I'd have a little standing desk in the back um that I'm getting through. So I'm trying to take notes. I'm trying to pay attention during the walkthroughs um but I can't even get on the practice field. And I think having the relationship I did with AB and and coach Stfansky when he was here. Um they knew like if it was game day and I can move a little bit, I was going to play. And so I think they had faith in me, especially after the first couple times the back went out. Um and so those were the toughest moments because you lose all the core, all the mobility and stuff and you're out there like I'm like I'm so stiff right now. Like I can't move. Like you're out there performing. But in my mindset until they told me I couldn't play, I was going to try and find a way to get out there. >> Yeah. Anybody who's listening who's had a back like backs suck. It affects everything. and sitting is hard, standing is hard. It doesn't it doesn't even matter. Then to go out there and try and play against guys who are maybe feeling a lot better than you and younger and more it's it it's it's awesome. I just want to say, you know, for me getting to know you, as I said at the beginning, has just been it it's been awesome. And you are, you know, in my mind like a Mount Rushmore guy that I've gotten to to meet in in my career here. And you are everything that I think anybody who roots for this team would want in a representative on the field and off the field. And it's awesome. I I remember like we do the Halloween costume for the for the kids. There aren't many people at your level who go to that and you do every did every single year and I always respect that. So you're just to me Jimmy said it I thought perfectly. You're an example perfect example of everything we want Clean Brown to be. So thank you so much man for all of it and getting to know you and be a part of your career as well while you're here. >> No I appreciate it. I mean, it it just being involved in the community and this team. Um, you want guys that it means something to and it means something to me. So, so I appreciate all all the kind words and uh, you know, being on on the show any chance I can get. >> Appreciate it, man. Thanks, Joel. >> Thanks. All right, we'll be back with more Clean Browns. We're going to go get a some tissues here. We'll back Browns Daily right after this. I believe the technical term is that was a lot going on today buddy here at the cross country mortgage campus. Lots going on. I believe you have that correct. Lot going on and also then a lot tonight. Big party. >> Luca Dragamir one years old. >> God, what are you going to get him? >> One year old. >> Well, we've got some some golf stuff for him. We've got some a little hoop for him. >> Oh, I love it. >> Yeah, we're getting them rolling. That's how I taught the boys how to walk was with that hoop. >> Is today actually the day of the day? Today's it. >> So, what I would do is I would I would stand them. You just had the dream. >> I have the ball in their hands in their hands and I would walk them to the hoop and then throw it in. And that that's how I taught all of them how to walk was with the mini hoop. The little hoop. >> Well, we'll be that's what we're working on. >> And then you're going to be hitting jumpers with him before you know it. >> Let's go. >> What a champion. The prince who was promised. >> I know. So fun. I also like how big of a deal is made of the first birthday and the kid remembers none of it. >> Yes. Oh, actually before when we get off the air, I'll show you a two second video that you're going to get a kick out of that I think will remind you very much of like Bootsie. >> That's great. That's fantastic. All right, kids. Uh day two of mandatory mini camp tomorrow. It will be a Deshawn Watson today. Uh it was a Shadur Sanders day today in terms of the reps with the one. So we'll see how Deshawn answers tomorrow on day two of mandatory mini camp. You have that to look forward to which is nice. Thanks for listening everybody. title: Joel Bitonio Press Conference | June 9th, 2026
text: You're going to sit over All right. Hello everybody. Thank you for coming today. Um, it's a really special day for the Cleveland Browns and our organization. I'll have to admit for the organization, Joel, it's a little bittersweet. Um, I think Joel Batonio embodies everything any team, but particularly the Cleveland Browns would value. Um, I would argue very strongly that he's a Hall of Fame player. And when you look at the what he achieved here, it compares very favorably to names like Jim Brown and Joe Thomas and Lou Groza, uh, in terms of quality of play, um, games played, etc. Um, we're excited for he and Courtney and their three little ones who are [clears throat] over here all appropriately adorned in 75 jerseys and they'll have their dad back full-time. Their dad is already slimmed down. He said he's not quite as slim as Joe Thomas, but he's headed in that direction, body feels better, etc. Uh, and we're also delighted at least for a year, Courtney, that and maybe longer that y'all are going to stay in the Cleveland area and that'll obviously you will always be a Cleveland Brown, but it helps when you live here. So, we're delighted about that. I think we'd be remiss if we didn't comment and just all of us go through what all Joel accomplished in his career. As you all know, he was a second round pick out of Nevada 12 years ago and immediately stepped in and started right next to Joe Thomas between Joe Thomas and Alex Max. So, that was a good place to start, Joel. Um, and early on had an injury, a foot injury if I remember. And I remember we were debating whether to extend him or not and could he stay healthy or not. And we obviously decided to extend him. And I don't think you ever missed a game again, did you? >> Um I'll look at my notes here. 178 career starts in his career. Um that's up there with Joe Thomas and Jim Brown. Um Joel made here's the most impressive thing and I think you all all know the difference. Joel made five Pro Bowls. Okay, five I'm sorry, five allp pro teams. Okay, five allp pro teams. And that's different than making the Pro Bowl. Okay, when you make the allpro team and twice he made the first team, that means he was one of the best one or two guards in the whole league. He did that twice. Three other times he made the second team. He made seven consecutive Pro Bowl teams. Okay, seven consecutive Pro Bowl teams. The only people to do that in our organization are the names I mentioned earlier, Jim Brown, Joe Thomas, and Luke Grosa. Okay. He was a model of consistency. I I hardly ever remember Joel having a bad game. Um he did what I think you ask everybody to do in any organization, and that is come to work, work hard, do your job, be a good team player, go home, spend time with your family, and come back and do it again. and he did that for 12 years. And you know, when players aren't in the building, there's a little bit of a tendency to forget about him. And when he and Courtney and the three kids got out of the car today, I thought, "Dang, I miss that guy." Because Joel was so reliable, showed up so often, uh, etc. So Joel is going to come up and make [clears throat] a few remarks, but I just want to emphasize I hope we can find more players in the future who are as good a players and as good a people as Joel Batonio because he embodies everything we want a Cleveland Brown to do. So with that, we'll introduce uh Joel Batonio, number 75, from the University of Nevada. So come on up here, big guy. [applause] got the good haircut, I say. >> Yeah. >> Well, I uh first off, I just appreciate everybody being here. Um I know it was a little short notice for some people. Um surprisingly, this has been in the works for, you know, a little while getting everybody's schedule on page and stuff like that. We uh you know, it took us a little while, but I appreciate the kind words, Mr. Hasslam. um D, you know, everything you guys have done for me and my family. Um, you know, it is like family here and and I appreciate that. So, I I prepared something. So, I'm gonna um, you know, try and read it and and try and stay focused. It's just a emotional time because it's what I've done, you know, my my whole adult life is has been here and been to Cleveland Brown. So, um, it's a big moment, but I'm going to I'm going to read some of these words to you guys and uh, you know, I appreciate you guys being here. When I reflect on my time as a Cleveland Brown, I'm so grateful. I've learned so much. After I was drafted, I had the unique experience of playing left guard in between 10 time Pro Bowl left tackle Joe Thomas and seventime Pro Bowl center Alex Mack. Um, what a way to learn how to be a pro in the NFL. I saw firsthand their toughness, their ability to play through injuries, the importance of being there for your teammates. I took that with me and did my best to instill that in my teammates. Later in my career, I sat next to John Greo in meetings. He taught me how to be a pro, take notes the right way, and play guard in the NFL. I was drafted the same year as Johnny Manzel, and we actually roommed together. I learned some things not to do from him. I got the opportunity to play with and learn from so many guys. I learned how to be eagleist from Nick Chub. I learned to always smile like Christian Kery. I learned a chief slam from David and Jooku. I learned how to be fiery and competitive from Baker. I learned selflessness from all my offensive lineman brethren. There are truly too many to name. Um and and the O line is just such a special special group. Um but you know just a special shout out to Mitch Schwarz, White Ter, Ethan Posick, Jack Conlin, Kevin Zitler, and the countless others. It was an honor to share the meeting room and the field with you men. I learned how to be detail oriented and always show up on game day for your teammates. Even if you didn't practice all week or ever from JC Treader, I got to experience pro balls with guys like Jarvis Landry Landry, Denzel Ward, Amari Cooper, Miles Garrett, JK, and Jerry Judy. I learned the feeling of pride that comes representing this organization among the greats of the NFL. And that's a feeling that never got old. I learned about the people behind the scenes who helped me help get the team ready for Sundays. The people in the building help helped make this place so special. Joe, Pat, Steph, and the training staff who would get me from being barely able to get out of my car on a Monday to ready to play on Sundays. Larry Jackson and his strength staff for the countless hours in the weight room, including Dale Jones for going above and beyond the second half of my career to help extend it. We always have our Friday morning lifts. Brad, Corey, Jimmy, and the equipment staff who always there for with any request. The cafeteria staff who kept us fed. The PR staff, including my guy Murf, who from day one had me ready for any questions the media threw at me. I learned about the Cleveland media, the seriousness of how they approach their jobs. I learned to just answer their questions as honestly as I could because it ultimately helped make the fans more interested. I learned just how hard it is to win in the NFL and how special the locker room is after those wins. Those are the moments I will never forget. I was always remember our Thursday night win against the Jets to open the fridges. I learned about serving the community. As athletes, we have a platform and have the opportunity to make a real difference for people. Giving back was something that my parents instilled in me. Those interactions with Browns Give Back, a kid again, the Cleveland Food Bank meant a lot to the kids and the people who we were able to help, but they also meant a lot to me, too. I encourage everyone to give back. [snorts] I learned about sacrifice and love from my wife Courtney, my kids Zoe, Benny, and Ada. I love you guys so much. Courtney has been on this journey with me since college and was truly the heartbeat of my career through the injuries, the wins, the losses. Always there, always supportive, and always my biggest fan. I learned how to compete and always try to win, even if it was racing to the car for my brother and sister. I learned true strength and love from my mom. Sometimes love is letting you know you shouldn't have fall started in the second quarter. I learned self-belief and hard work from my dad. who never got to see me play a snap in college or the NFL, but was with me every step of the way. He believed in me and my dreams before I knew what they were. He would tell me, "Why not you?" whenever I brought up how hard it was to make it in college or the NFL. So, if he's listening right now, I just wanted to let him know we made it. I learned how to be appreciative. Thank you to the Hen family, to all my teammates, to the coaches, to Andrew Barry, to [snorts] anyone who believed in me, to the fans who supported us. Thank you to everyone I was able to learn from. I learned to appreciate everyone who helped me on this amazing journey. I learned what an honor and a privilege it is to wear to be able to wear that orange helmet and what this team means to the fans. I learned how hard it is to say goodbye. I had a good idea back in January that this was the end for me, but this place is so special that it was hard to truly say goodbye. I'm so glad I got to learn and be a Cleveland Brown my entire career. Thank you. So why was it so important for you to stay here to finish your career here even through all the losing and the hard times and the coaches and the quarterbacks? >> Yeah, I was always appreciative of um you know the team drafting you. Uh you know I got I got picked in the second round and and I played here and early in my career they trusted me even I know I was injury you know Mr. has them, you know, said like there was a question, you know, and and I wanted to always prove him right and and by the time we got things rolling where we made the playoffs and we're having these runs. Um I was kind of in, you know, year seven, eight, nine in my career. And um and by that point, like you're so committed, you put in so much work here. I was ready to see it through and I was ready to see, you know, the ultimate goal was to to win a Super Bowl and that that was my goal here. Um, but once you once you get through it, like for me, I could never just picture myself in a different uniform. >> Were there overtures made to you from other teams? >> Um, never anything serious. I I I know my agent talked to a bunch of teams, you know, during the combine and everything and people asked if I was interested in and continue to play, like what my plan was. Um, but there never got anything um where I was telling people I wanted to play for another team. When made you decide to retire now, Joel? >> Um, well, like I said a little bit earlier, the decision was was made like me and Andrew Barry had a conversation before free agent. I think you guys we signed like three interior linemen on the first day of free agency. So, um, that was kind of like me and AB had already discussed that I was, you know, going to retire and I I was I was finishing up my career. It was really just the timing of the announcement. Um, you know, I talked to my agent and and he's like, I mean, technically, you don't have to say anything. Like, you're re retired and he's like, I I've been playing football for 23 years of my life and here for 12 years and you just want to make sure it's done. I never wanted to be the guy that was like, all right, I'm I'm done playing, but now I want to go make another run at it and come back and unretire. Um, and so for me it was just, hey, we want to have a a finite decision, but we were in constant communication with the team and and and they I I appreciate them understanding and uh, you know, I'm sure AB had to answer a few questions where he he knew the answer to, but um, but I appreciate that. >> Joe, you football's been your life. I mean, even the last college, the last 12 years. Have you thought about what the next chapter? I mean, what the next chapter holds for you? what you you know you want to do. >> Um not exactly. I mean spend some time with the family. Um you know they are ready and eager and and uh be there for them. Enjoy some of the holidays. You know you don't get uh you know you miss Thanksgiving you know parts of Thanksgiving and Christmas and and those things. I think all that stuff will be very cool. Um but for me on like a professional level I haven't I haven't really dove into you know exactly what I I want to do. When when the the Bronx finally made the playoffs on with you playing, there was the co game and you had to miss the Pittsburgh game. >> You had to sweat that out for them to win to see your first playoff game. What was that game like for you watching it? >> Yeah, it was. Well, thank goodness it was a route. Like the Browns kick some butt. Um, you know, after the first snap, I was just like, "All right, we we you know, we got a chance here." You don't know. I mean, we're missing Denzel. Like, there was a lot of guys that were out. Coach Stfansky. Um, and so, but being a fan is is brutal. Um, I was I was definitely sweating and and I was uh it was unbelievable that my neighborhood like knew I was at home and they started lighting off fireworks after the game and they threw like a little parade down the street. So, it was it was an unbelievable experience because, you know, we got the win. I think it would have been heart-wrenching if you're sitting there and and the team loses. >> Joel, you said in that letter you wrote this morning that you'd never been here before they drafted you, right? you didn't come out and visit. So, why do you think you made such a connection with this comedian, this fan base, and I think as quickly as you did, but then throughout your 12 years? >> Yeah, I you know, I am from Southern California, but I think if you look at my background and family, like it's based off of like bluecollar, hard work. Um, and I think at heart, like there's some Midwest in there, you know what I and you come to Cleveland and the people here, you know, accept you. And like I said, I got to play next to Joe and Alex and Greck and Schwarz and um they just showed me what it was like to be a pro. And I I think I wanted to throw myself in it 100%. And I was committed and I was like, hey, I want to be the best version of myself, which is hopefully in turn going to help the team. Um and so that was really kind of my mindset. And then, you know, once you connect with the community and you have all your kids here and you you know, they go to school and you're you're part of it, you know, and so you you're rooting for it, too. And um we'll always be fans, you know, of the Browns and and the community and and the people, our neighbors, like it's just a special place for us. >> What do you think you miss most about being a Browns player? >> Oh gosh. Um I think it's the people. Like, you know, you you walk in the building and I've been here with like players come and go, right? But they're they're the people in there at the locker room. The celebrations after the wins are there's nothing because you put so much work in. You only have 17 opportunities a year. And so every time we got a win, I I celebrated full fully because, you know, I went so long at parts of my career where we weren't winning consistently. Um but it's the people you work with, the training staff, the strength staff, the EQ staff, like like the heads of those departments were interns when I got here and now they're, you know, running the departments. And so I feel like we grew up together and like those are your people that you see on a daily basis and they know the work that goes behind it like like there was times where it was like I'm not walking on Monday and Tuesday and it's like are we going to find a way to play and you know you have to have those people that you connect with um and that help push you through those those moments. >> You talked you talked so much over your career about just Joe what he's meant to you how he passed things on to you and others who have passed things on to you. I know it's a lot of young, a lot of new on this roster, but as you sort of leave, what's maybe the thing that you hope you left your mark on for the the sort of new generation players that are coming in? >> I think just consistency, like being being who you are each and every day. And it's a business, right? Like the NFL is such a business, but I think if you peel it back and you're the best version of yourself and you give everything you can in the moment every day and you have a bunch of guys that want to do that, like it builds up the culture and it builds up the what the team is and who who they want to be. And so if people just see that like, hey, that guy came to work, you know, win or loss, like he was who he is and he put in the work and was ready on Sundays to uh to give his best. to me like I think that's how you build a culture of winning. How >> were you able to maintain such a positive attitude week in week out, year in year out through all the losing? I mean, I remember Joe Thomas saying that it really got to him emotionally, but you just were, you know, you just seemed like you were always there with a smile on your face and you kept the locker room up and fans up and gave everyone some hope. How did you do that? >> Yeah, losing is not easy. like everybody plays the game to win the game, but I I feel like I woke up in the mornings and I was like, I'm playing in the National Football League, you know, for the Cleveland Browns and I get to go to work and I'm healthy and I'm playing in these games. Um, and so that was special. It was just a moment. It's like what you dream of as a kid and you're living your dream. Um, and like I do think positive vibes are contagious, right? Like if you're a positive person, like hopefully that rubs off on some people. Um, but to me it was like I was living a dream every day that I got to come into this building and uh and be a part of it. And the ultimate goal was to try and, you know, lift a Super Bowl. And that's why I tell people like the best moments were going to those playoffs cuz we were getting closer and and um, you know, you wanted more of those moments, but like those wins and those locker rooms made up for all the uh, tough days you had. Speaking of gohead, >> I want to speak for the group for a second and say we appreciate all the times in the quiet empty locker room that you've stayed and answered questions and I think one in particular the walk back to the press box in New Orleans in 24 where like this guy can't ever retire. [laughter] We need it. But is that something that came natural to you and why was it important for you to always step up and do that? Yeah, I I think for me our PR team, Dan, you know, included, PJB, always made it a point like it's like it's your guys' job to obviously tell a story about what happened. It's our job to give you guys information to help help write that story, but if we can control the narrative in the sense of, hey, I was out there. I experienced it. I played the game, and if there is something I need to take blame for, I can. You know what I mean? And I'm not passing blame to anybody else. And it's it's with this Twitter and Instagram world, the longer you take not to answer a question, um the more it it goes. I mean, even just like in this retirement, like there's crazy stories about if I'm going to play somewhere or not. And you know, we just kind of kept it quiet, but um there's just so many moments where I played in the game. I'm a captain of this team. Like I can talk to the media and I can answer the questions. >> Think about the last two years in particular. I know you had like some nagging injuries going on, the back in particular that we talk to you about all the time, but you know, through that and the combined eight wins over those two years. Um, how important was it for you to play in all those games that you did? And is that something you look back on without regret now? >> Yeah, there was never regret in a game I played in. Um, but I wanted to be there. There was a couple times, especially I think this last year where it was close and I was I was uh unc uncertain, but I was like I'm at a point now like I'm I'm out there. I can move a little bit. And it might have been the wrong mindset for me, but like I was like Joel being out there at 70% or 60% is like good enough for me and I'm I'm going to go out there and try and compete. Um, and so that that that was kind of my mindset and the win loss thing like never had a on my it was always just a personal opinion and I talked to the training staff about it. I was like, we make decisions on Monday if we're going to play or not. And it's not true, but it's just the mindset you have, right? You walk in, they're like, hey, this is what you got going on. And it's like, all right, well, I got to figure out a way to play. And so that's the mindset switches when you walk in the door on Monday. And I just always tried to have that that mindset. Um, but the win losses to me it it was just that's who I am as a person. Like you can't change who you are you winning or losing and that's kind of just the way I I I stuck through it. >> Jimmy and Andrew and Joe Thomas mentioned you with the Hall of Fame. Like how do you view your candidacy and how important would that be to you? >> I mean it'd be unbelievable important. It's like the pinnacle of like the individual achievement of a a football player. Um I never had a goal to be like a gold jacket guy. I just wanted to go out and be the the best I could. Um, it's my like yearly appointment that there's not enough guards and setters in the Hall of Fame. I think if you look at it, there's there's so many elite players. And if you look at Pro Bowls and all pros compared to quarterbacks, I know there's difference importance on positions, but receivers, tight ends, like any other position group, if you look at the actual accolades of players, like there needs to be more guards and centers in the Hall of Fame. Um, and so I think that's a barrier just being a guard. Um, but I I think if you want to look at consistency and you want to look at longevity and and um the history of the franchise and some of the names that, you know, Mr. Ham mentioned today, um, I'm proud of my career and I I I would love, like I said, to be in the Hall of Fame someday, but I don't need it to like any personal thing like that. I'm happy with what I've done and and um I'm proud of that. >> You play with 24 different quarterbacks. It's even more than Joe did. Um, for any particular reason, is there a favorite that you'll remember? >> Oh gosh, in the moments, I mean, it was great. Like my rookie year having Hoyer back there, like that was a heck of a run when we were, you know, seven and four and I I didn't know any better, but I was just like, "All right, this is the NFL. Like, we're we're flying around. Let's do this." That was great. Obviously, um, you know, Josh Macauen was just like so wise when he was fun to play with him. uh Baker obviously changed our trajectory of our franchise there and like led us to the playoffs and that was that was unbelievable. um in that letter that was, you know, some of the coolest moments of my career is is that season even though it was it was COVID, but making that run um was awesome. And then, you know, you bring in uh Joe Flacco all you hear these stories, you play against him a bunch of times and then you meet him as a person, you're like, "All right, this guy's a pretty pretty cool guy." Um and so I mean, you take something from everybody you play with, right? But I think those were kind of like just certain points in the career when we were winning the most games and and that's when the uh best memories usually come from. >> Family, you mentioned it a couple times. So I want to just ask you like when you're when you're making your decision, how much of it was it about like it's the right time for you, but also for Courtney and the kids? Yeah, I mean Courtney's so supportive and uh I'm sure she would tell you she wants me at home more, but I guarantee if I was like, "Hey, I wanted to play another season." Like, she would be 100% supportive of of that decision. But it's great. I I mean, I don't have to tell the kids I can't wrestle because my back's hurting or or something like that. So, we should have some uh some more free time. But, it's it's a part of it. But, truthfully, the decision came down to like my body. Am I going to be able to prep the way I wanted to prep to to be able to perform at the level I wanted to perform at? >> Oh gosh. Um I went to school for economics. Um but I don't know. I might have like coached if I had just played in college. I I enjoy the game. Like I I love, you know, football and the scheme and all that stuff. Um but I didn't have a I didn't have a rightway backup plan. You know, I did some architectural stuff in high school that I really enjoyed. Nevada did not have an architecture program, but um but yeah, I don't know. It would be uh interesting. >> What do you think the next couple months are going to be like knowing you don't have to prepare for a training camp and rigor of the season? >> I think um I was, you know, telling my wife the other day that like it still kind of feels like an offseason right now. Like I I've still been working. I'm obviously not training as much, not at mini camp right now. But I think when training camp starts is going to be the real moment like, okay, I'm retired from this because that's when, you know, se end of July, August, September when everything really cranks up. Um, so we'll see how it feels. Um, I'm sure there's emotions going in there. I tell you what, like the stress of getting ready for a game and wanted to perform at your best, I I don't know if I'll miss that. Um, you know, even going into year 12, like every night before the game, you're you're stressed about your assignment and and as an offensive lineman, like you're protecting people out there and so you want to play your best and uh and be the best version of yourself. >> Obviously, you know, we'll all share our memories of you or whatever, but just in your own words, how would you like to be remembered? >> Yeah, ju just um I poured myself into it. I was, you know, 100% committed to this this team and and this organization. And I truly always wanted to be the best version of myself. Um to help make the team as good as we could be. And and that that's what I pushed for. And um that's what, you know, I hope people remember this guy was tough. He was going to be out there. He was going to fight for his teammates and um and was just a consistent guy. >> It's a really tough trying to follow Joe Thomas just in terms of voice of the team, face of the team, spokesperson, uh, anchor of the line and all of those things. Did you feel a tremendous amount of responsibility when Joe passed you that torch? And how do you feel like you handled it? >> Um, it was I mean Joe Thomas is obviously like if not one of the best left tackles in in the game. So Andy was a great leader and and a great spokesperson. Um, I think it helped me because I saw him do it at such a high level that I was like, "All right, I gotta, you know, step into those and I would never, you know, compare myself to what he did." Um, but just just step in and be like, "All right, someone needs to do that for the team and kind of be a part of it." So, it was never a pressure thing, but I did think it helped and kind of showed a way of how if it even if the season doesn't go great, you can still be a professional and, you know, handle handle your job. when you when you had those injuries early [snorts] in your career, you know, two straight years ending on IR, did did you ever kind of wonder like what this would be and then did it make it more meaningful kind of to to have that iron man streak? >> Yeah, you know, and I had really never been injured in my career like I never miss any college games or any high school games. So, I was like when I was missing games, I was like this is weird, you know, and I was playing next to Joe Thomas who never missed games. Alex Mack who for a majority of his career had not missed games. And so I was like, man, this is this is weird. In the back of my mind, I always like it's unlucky. Like I got rolled up on twice and I got stepped on. Like that's how my injuries occurred. U but at some point like in the back of your mind you're like, is this part of it? You know, what do I need to do differently? And and um I think once we got on a roll there and it was like seven years without missing a snap, I was like, "All right, I I think there is some luck to this, you know, part of it and and I'm just going to go out there and do a thing." But I definitely was questioning um a little bit of like injury luck and and what was going on. But I think the Browns also having confidence in me and still extending me and and being in that position to be like we want this guy around. Um gave me some confidence as well. >> You mentioned that you your agent filled some calls from other teams and you mentioned your conversations with Andrew and were you kind of made your intentions known. Did you have any conversations with Todd George Warhop and if so how much did they try to sell you on coming back? What was their sort of pitch to you? >> Yeah, I went up uh I went up and met him because I was rehabbing my elbow. I had a little elbow clean up. Um, and I was rehabing my elbow. So, when they got hired, I went up there. I mean, I I know Coach Monkin from when he coached here, obviously. And then I've only heard good things about George Warhop, like from Joe and Alex and Mitch. Like, they all love him as a O line coach. And so, I went up and talked to him and uh they were pretty clear. They're like, "Hey, we want you back if you want to play football." So, it it was very cut and dry, but like they were like, "Yes, this is he's like, "We want you in the room if you can do it." and and you know, coach Min talked about the Baltimore game where I chased down that interception, you know, and he's like, even though you guys were losing and stuff and and he's just like, we we want those type of people, you know, in the building. And so, it was just a open communication of of, hey, like we would like you back if you want to keep playing. But it was definitely they understood, you know, where I was coming from on my decision. Is there a specific opposing player that you've gone against that maybe >> you're going to remember remember most? >> I mean, you think about like the AFC North guys, right? Like Cam Hayward, he was probably in year three when I got in the league and he's still playing football. So, like we battled over 20 times and he predominantly lines up over the left guard, left tackle. Um, so that's one. I mean, early in my career, Gino Atkins was a headache. Like, you know, Aaron Donald is in a class of his own, but Gino Atkins was like the mini version of that, you know, and he was unbelievable. So, I think those two from like a a a North comparison would be the two. >> Sticking around here for a year, I think says a lot about how you feel about the city of Cleveland and how you, I'm guessing, were embraced here. So, uh, what makes this so special and you know, how much does this really end up like home to you. >> Yeah, it's a big part. Um, you know, 12 years is a long time, right? Like we, you know, I'm like, all right, I moved out of the house at 17 to go to college. I'm like, I'm almost, you know, at 12, you know, almost there in in Cleveland. Um, it's a big part and and part of football is you kind of miss the whole fall and the Christmas time and stuff. And we were like, you know, let's let's enjoy some time here and and be a fan and be a Cleveland person. Like there's, you know, we live in Avon, but like it's just a small town feel, you know what I mean? in that and and you don't get that vibe necessarily back in California all the time. Um so we wanted to enjoy it, be a fan uh you know, be a fan of the Browns and kind of just um so yeah, but it's a huge part of it. Like I said, our we'll always have, you know, this will always be part of our our family. You know, our kids are all born in Cleveland like and that that's that's a huge huge thing. Um you know, I proposed in Cleveland, so like every you know, it's it's going to be a huge part of our life and you know, we'll drive by and be like, "Oh, that was you know, our house someday." But no, we're going to enjoy it and and try and uh I mean, you can't beat this weather last like two and a half weeks, right? This is like Cali weather. Got humid for mini camp, of course. But >> we'll be weird watching. >> We're take two more. >> We'll be weird watching Browns games on TV. >> Yeah, I think it will be at the start for sure. You know, I think you're going to be like, "Oh man, I'm used to being out there. I'm used to playing." But um but I'll I'll be I'll be cheering them on >> around the current guys and this new team and what they've been doing with mini camp, but just what they're building here, what you're leaving team's a lot younger obviously on both sides of the ball and the future obviously looks bright, but what did you see in a players perspective of this team right now as you depart? >> Yeah, I'm still in communication with a lot of the guys. Um and I think coach Monkin is is is building that culture. like you said, there's a lot of young talented players that are are going to step into those leadership roles and and and keep forming, but I think they're working very hard from what I've heard, what I've seen. Lots of plays in practice. Um, you know, and that's how you get better. Like it's sometimes when you got a old team, it's hard to hard, you know what I mean? Like not all the guys are able to. Um, but when you're young, it's like let's run the ball out and get as many reps as you can. So, I think they're they're building that culture and I have uh like I said, I have nothing but respect for the coaching staff and like none of that was ever part of the decision. It was strictly like a physical thing, but I think there's a culture here. I think um the young talent that's been acquired over the last couple years is is impressive and I'm I'm looking forward to the future. >> Thanks everyone. >> Yeah, thanks guys. Appreciate it. We're gonna take a couple photos. We'd love to get the family with a photo of Joel.

title: Dion Dawkins Meets With Media At Bills Minicamp | Buffalo Bills
text: It's been a while for you in this league. How you feeling coming into this season? >> Feel good. You know, I I definitely >> I definitely don't feel like a vet, but I'm definitely feeling like a vet. You know, being around for a long time. Like, you could definitely tell you've been around for a long time. But the good thing is that my body I don't feel like that I've been around for a long time, you know? Like I got good people in my corner that help, you know. Only thing and with me is is weight. weight goes up and weight and goes down, you know. And what I've learned is over the duration of a career, you have to just monitor your eating and just understand that your body can't take some of the same things of intake that you used to might have done when you were younger. But besides that, ball is ball. Snow is snow. >> What's it been like first significant coaching change at the top for you? And you've been here the longest. You've been with Shawn the longest and now it's there is something that's different. What's that been like? >> I mean, we just got a new guy leading the the the team meetings, right? Like there's a new guy leading the team meetings, Joe Brady. And uh the energy is just it's just different, right? Like it I hate that, you know, it's like, oh, new this and new that. Like cuz we all love Shawn, you know, like we all and love Shawn. Sean is our dog. But you know, like in this business, things happen and we have a new guy in charge now. And the and the flow is definitely a different flow. You know, Brady is Brady's younger. He understands a little more. And Brady's from Florida, right? So, we got a different a different energy source. You know, like Sean's a wrestling guy, Joe Brady's not. You know, Sean's a PA guy, Joe Brady's not. So, it's two totally different guys, but uh they both are great and they both are doing a good job. I know that McDermad is down in Carolina. Brady's here and uh everything's going well so far. >> What's it like for you at this stage of your career to have such a a change? >> Never been in that change. So, I don't know. I don't know. You know, it's only been what, seven weeks of the offseason or eight weeks. So, the first eight weeks have been great. Joe Brady has been doing a great job and uh I'm proud of him because, you know, like to be a coach, a head coach in this league, it's extremely hard. Just like how it's hard to be a left tackle, it's hard to be a quarterback. you know, like we're all employees of of the NFL and it's hard to be an employee of the NFL or work for the NFL. So, um, I tip my hat to him. I respect the guy. He's coming here, no hiccup, looked everybody in the face and hit the ground running. You know, he works us hard, we practice hard, we lift hard, and he demands a lot out of guys. And, you know, we all are adapting for a different type of way that is going on here. But, it's it's been fun. A lot of guys are hyped. guys are still able to be in their self. So, I love it. I'm still able to walk around but the locker room and make noises and and you already know. So, I haven't had no bad looks or no bad eyebrows. So, you know, I love it here still. >> Are you where you want to be? There's been a lot of talk about physically where you want to be, where you want to play, your weight, things like that. Are you where you want to be right now? >> Of course not. Why would I be where I'm supposed to be? The season just ended like two months ago. No, you know, but I'm definitely on the right track. Definitely on the right track. Can't you tell? Little chisel. Know what I'm saying? But uh it's been going well. It's just work, man. It's just work. You know, like you like we are masters of our bodies, right? So every year you you put your body do through different things and I've chose to put my body through a different thing and this year, you know, like I got goals and I want to be in the best left tackle for Josh Allen and for my team and for myself. So, um, if every year I've been playing at a certain weight and this year I chose to play at a different weight. So, whether it's 5 lbs lighter or 5 lbs heavier, you know, I chose to be different in body composition in this year. So, that's what I'll fight for throughout the whole season. >> Dian, what do you feel like you guys have accomplished as a team over the last couple months? >> Brotherhood. It feels like we've been a team for a year and a half already. Like look, Shavers is riding around on Alex bike, you know? Like guys don't let guys borrow stuff like that, you know? Like it's just a bunch of dudes, man. Like not that it feels like college, but like the like the bond, it feels like a college bond. Like everybody like literally hangs out and that's all that you can ask for cuz like in the league, you know, everybody kind of does their own thing and goes their own way. But for a team that really like wants to be around like one another organically, Maddie, it's a it's a cool thing and it's beautiful to to to honestly see because the Bills like we have a rumor, not a rumor, but like we have a a rapport that the rest of the league knows like it's just like, oh, like they they're a tight group of guys in Buffalo. They're a tight group. And then when guys like come here and then they really see that, yeah, we are a freaking tight group of guys and then it just keeps developing in the right way. So tight group is definitely still going and I'm happy that it is cuz it's hard to grow a team and it's hard to, you know, bond with a bunch of different men from different places, especially older guys that come in and young guys that had a million dollars in in college to guys that just made the team for the first time, you know, like it's a it's a drastically different world, but the bond is still strong. >> I saw a video of you a couple days ago. Boy, >> you were in the you were in the new stadium. >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Trying to make >> I've been here like every day. I love it. What are you most excited about? And is it weird coming here and seeing the other one go down? >> Nope. Nope. Nope. Nope. Nope. It ain't weird at all. I can't wait. You know, like uh the old stadium, it did what it had to to do, you know, like that old stadium did exactly what it had to do. And being in that new stadium, and I got so many videos that I'm going to keep posting, too. So, um the new stadium is is amazing, right? And it's literally like a a brand new Tesla truck in a desert. Like it's almost like it's not supposed to be here, but it's here. Like you go in a stadium and I'm telling you, like like you look up like this. Like you look up, right? And there's fans like that way. Literally, not this way, but that way. And it's like it seems like everything is above you. And I got to press the the train horn, all that stuff. Yo, y'all know me. I'm a big kid, right? And that like that stuff is fun. and to be able to go in there and just admire it, but also knowing all of the blood, sweat, and tears and people that, you know, started their careers and ended their careers and things that happened there and good things and bad things, you know, but for what is going on here, bro, it's time for something new, right? Not and and not to say that it's time for new players, but it's time for something new. And if something new was that stadium, shoot, I'm here for it. You know that like the locker room is crazy. title: Josh Allen On Bills Minicamp | Buffalo Bills
text: Yeah, I think we're coming out here. We're competing at a very high level. Guys are flying around. Um we've done a good job of connecting. These are the couple of the miles that as you hear our guys cheering on each other. Um couple of the things that Joe had wanted for this OTA period to be is uh you know, connect, compete, condition, um and then come out here and just have a lot of fun and uh play some football. >> Where are you as far as like chemistry with DJ? >> Still working on it. Um still working on with everybody, you know? There's just different nuances that some guys have in their body language. Um he's as smooth of of a football player as I've ever been around. Um and it's just, you know, I'm lucky to come to work and and have the guys that we do, especially him going out there and and he works extremely hard. Um you know, it's fun to fun to be out there with him. >> What's it like having a new coach? Obviously you're familiar with your team and so forth, but what's it like having him as your new guy >> Yeah, I mean uh no stranger to to coach and um to have the familiarity that I do with him and to to have the relationship that I do, to bounce different ideas off of him. Um you know, he's still our play caller. That's not going to change and I think his uh his wants or emotions during practice have changed a little bit cuz he's got to he's got to root for both sides now, um which is awesome to see. He's going out there. He's he's cheering our defense on. He's cheering our offense on. And uh he just wants us to go out there and like I said earlier, compete as as hard as we can. >> What's the process look like of building a relationship with the partner being important? >> Yeah, it's just uh a lot of meeting time. Um you know, that's kind of what this OTA is is for as well. You're kind of reinstalling the playbook and it may be the same type of playbook that I've been in for the last 8 years, but a lot of different nuance this year and he he brings a lot of knowledge from his previous stops in the league. Um he's got a lot of experience and to be able to again talk through different concepts, different defenses, uh how he sees it and how he conveys it to us. He's doing a great job in our room and we're lucky to have him. >> What's it like when you drive in and you see the old stadium being torn down when you drive in? And the memories and that sort of thing and then you turn around and you drive out and you see the new stadium. What sort of goes through your mind when you sort of see all that happening? >> Yeah, I think you know, my mind my my eyes are more attracted to the other one. I see that a little bit more. Uh obviously a lot of memories in the old I'm not too too much of a sentimental guy, so um you know, this place has got grass and it's going to be pretty cool in there. I've been in there a few times and I think the fans are going to be very pleased when when we get that place rocking. >> Josh, what's it been like going up against C.J. Gardner-Johnson? >> Uh it's been awesome. Um he's a he's a competitor. he's the loudest guy in in the room at all times. Uh you know, he's a constant constant competitor and um you know, nothing that he does is half speed. He does it full speed and to have a guy like that in your locker room pushing your guys and and forcing them to compete even harder. It's Those guys are are gems and I think every team needs that type of guy. >> Josh, what is it like What is it like being back to work with James and >> Uh just I mean, business as usual. Um he's a you know, he's he's the best back in in the league. Comes out here and hasn't missed a step and it's just as you know, we got to see him do what he did last year and um he's a tremendous talent, tremendous player, tremendous teammate and we just love having him back. >> Josh, are you even though you coached the time in between, is it different with your body or anything or is it more similar to the now? >> Uh similar routine, spend a little bit more time on on the body, um working out and and just trying to continue to hone in on the mechanic side of things. I feel like I'm in a good spot right now and um can on can can still be better. So, I'm going to continue to find ways that I can do that. Um but I actually having a baby now sticking around the house a little bit more and trying to balance you know being a dad and going out there and getting my work done too. So, it's it's still awesome though. >> What's the dynamic? >> What How was your approach to balance? You know, it's a whole another >> I'll I'll let you know when it happens, you know. >> Is there anything like do you ask people like lay down or like what do you like >> Um I mean you can ask questions but until you kind of go through it yourself, you never know and um you know, when I have this next you know, 6 weeks off or whatever we however long it is, you have to find your schedule and what what works for you and um we'll go from there. >> What's it been like Aaron Kromer was here for so long leading the offensive line. What's it been like kind of watching them grow under a new tutelage? >> It's awesome. You know, coach coach Myers doing a great job. Um love his energy. I love talking with him. Actually, we miss Chrome too. Um but he's doing such a great job. He's got a lot of really good relationships in that room already. Um you know, having not been in his room all that much. We haven't really had many uh you know, protection meetings yet just cuz we're not in that mode but I'm excited to get in there and and and hear how he teaches and the guys are responding extremely well to him. Um so, that's a obviously a plus. >> Your number nine. >> It's crazy. >> I mean yeah, when you think of that number, what's it mean to you? >> Um again a lot of a lot of hard work. Um you know, you don't I don't know. It's just it's cool, I guess. I don't know. I don't really think about it too much. It feels like I'm still in year three or four and the the time does fly by and uh just trying to enjoy every moment of it. >> Josh, how how How does practice feel with a new defense, the new scheming and all of that, just from your perspective? >> Yeah, it's uh I mean a lot of a lot of movement, a lot of uh just flashes in in your eyesight. Um they're doing a great job of flying around and making it hard for the offense and trying to depict what they're in before before the play happens and it's it's hard to do against this defense. So, um your pre-snap reads have to be spot-on and if they're not, your post-snap reads have to be even better um and allow you to put the ball where you need to put it. >> Um we're doing a summer reading thing and I was curious if there's any books maybe you're reading with your daughter or like any books you're planning to read with this summer. >> Oh, The Pout-Pout Fish. That's a good one right now. She likes that one. >> Cool.

title: Joe Brady Speaks To The Media Before Minicamp | Buffalo Bills
text: Joe, do you expect everyone to be here for mentor? >> Everybody's here. >> Good. >> I'm good. Uh yeah. No, everybody everybody's here. Uh um yeah, we've had I mean we've had great attendance this whole offseason, so I'm really pleased with our uh just the way the guys are competing and excited for uh these next couple days. >> Do you wish James had been here for more of it? >> I mean, look, uh you guys saw how James wasn't here last offseason and and I always want our guys here, right? And, um, I give him a lot of credit. You go back to the offseason he had last year that that he was able to withstand, you know, that and you knew going into it how many times he was going to run the ball and it wasn't like he's he's not taking hits. Um, James was just playing at such a high level last year and he was in such a rhythm and a routine that, um, you know, I felt confident in him being able to kind of hold uphold that. And so, a great opportunity for them. Dorian Williams. >> Yeah. No, Dorian. Look, Dorian uh um you guys said Dorian's, you know, he did get injured. Um but Dorian's handling everything the right way and he'll be ready to go. There's been some guys that have practiced and haven't. Joe, how much more he does settled do you feel in the head coaching position now that you run practices and been in that role four months? >> Yeah, I don't know. I'm I'm be lying if I've spent a lot of time thinking about it, right? I just kind of wake up and see what I got to do to attack the day and um but I I like I like the direction that our team is going right now and the way that they're competing with each other and um you know, just kind of doing everything we're asking right now. title: Antonio Johnson & Ventrell Miller Talk Confidence Built by Trust | Media Availability
text: What was it like kind of watching Devin Lloyd, obviously not kind of stay, and and then bring him back, and and now this opportunity kind of opens up for you? >> Mhm. Uh I know it was a business a business thing that went down. Uh said he uh left got him a good pay payday. Um but like I said, the the opportunity is open for me, and I'm excited to see what that's about. >> Knowing that the Jazz front office didn't go and necessarily get another guy in free agency, what did that kind of say to you? >> Uh gave me a little bit of confidence coming into OTAs that they believe in the group we got right now. Uh group of guys. Um so, gave me some confidence in that. >> Yeah, how much does that impact you when you come out here and be like, "Okay, these guys clearly see something in me" and there's a bit of confidence there? >> Mhm. Uh just excited to uh to go prove them right from my perspective. Uh but like I said, it's just the confident they gave me the confidence, and just feels good that your coaching staff believes in you. >> What is kind of the biggest thing that you're working on and trying to nail down this off-season? >> Uh I would say like no enemies. Uh always trying to be perfect, be perfect in my game, my technique, be perfect executing the call, um and flying around and trying to make plays within that. >> How are you approaching with your mindset this season? Are you approaching this season any different than the previous ones? >> Uh I feel like there's a little bit more at stake for me, but uh always locked in. Um looking at more film. Um trying to be trying to be trying to be great. So, all that working working trying to get better. Um I would say that's pretty much pretty much it. >> How do you feel health-wise? I feel like you've had some injuries you've battled through before. And coming and also to have a system that you've worked through last year, do you feel like that gives you a leg up as well? >> Uh yeah, definitely. Uh coming in second year with this scheme, feeling feeling feeling confident with it. Uh and just feeling good really uh body-wise for real. Coming off I know I had some previous injuries, but feeling good right now, and like I said, just confident coming into the second year of the the same scheme. >> I feel like a lot of players like playing for Camp because he allows them to kind of be their best self, right? And play to their strengths. Do you feel that way on this defense? >> Uh yeah, most definitely. Uh no, coach can't hard on me. Always wanting me to get better. Uh Like I said, he always trying to find two things within me. So, just having a coach just stay on you, trying to push you to be the be the best version of yourself, that's always comes in handy. Help you to be great. >> This team had a lot of success last year, but I don't feel like anybody really talks about it as much. Has it been easy to turn the page after, you know, you guys saw a lot of success last year, but that doesn't mean anything this year? >> Oh, yeah, most definitely. I feel like they coaches style did a good job. Coach Lynn did a good job of saying it regardless of what happened last year, it's a new year. So, just getting your mind right for what we what can we do this year, being the best version we can this year, and trying to trying to go win games. >> Last season, it was playing between you and Devin for that starting spot. He obviously then went on to have that standout year. What did you learn from that experience? I say really all I guess all it takes is a year. Um But, I say just just uh staying staying the course, staying the course you can get good things to come by that. Continue to work hard regardless of what the circumstances may be. And you see that like you said, if you do the right thing, you you being put in the right position, you can make a lot of plays in this in this defense. >> Obviously, Gaters new head coach. What do you think of John Sumrall and what he's doing down there? >> Uh I'm excited about him. He bringing a lot of energy down there. Excited to see what he does. I heard a lot of good things about him. Probably go check him out during this little month off down there, but I'm excited to see what he does for sure. >> Okay, how are you? How was your off season? What what did you get to out of the off season? >> I've just been chilling with family. Me, Dorian, Jay Lou, and Buster. We we all train together in Dallas this off season. So, you know, just trying to get that chemistry together. And so, we come back here and we could be all on one accord. >> How does Vio coming back now first day of mini camp is complete? >> I feel great. You know, just being out here with the guys. Going into year two in the same defensive scheme. It's a little It's It's a different feel than last year. Everybody moving faster. We kind of understand what's the objective of each defense. So, like we can kind of like play with it a little bit, give the quarterback a different look knowing what we're going to get into, so it's just a different look if you're looking into the defense this year. >> Anthony talked about you last week and he said, kind of echoing the same sentiments you just mentioned, but also saying this year you're able to teach the younger guys, you're more of a communicator this year. How have you seen your role taking over down here in your junior year? >> Yeah, it's crazy cuz now I'm the older guy like one of the older guys in the room, so just having that confidence and having the younger guys being confident in me to come ask questions and look at ask me as a leader in the room. It's a little different, but I'm enjoying it at the same time. I just remember like when I was a young guy, so I never really been the older guy in the room since like high school. So cuz I've always been there's always been older guys, you know, in the room with me, so it's a little different, but I love it. >> Did you take some time to look back at last year and kind of, you know, obviously had a breakout season for yourself personally, but did you have some time to look back and like see the growth that you made? >> I most definitely, um really each week, each week I feel like each game, each practice week I grew, I learned a lot um from the older guys in the room and just from like the experience of being out there. So um when the season was over with, you know, I went back and watched plays and watched games and just understood that like I was just like, oh I wish I could make this play or cuz like I understand what I'm looking at now, so I'm like, okay, this year I'm I'm looking forward to be able to be able to go out there and just, you know, play freely and have a lot of fun. >> Um you guys are such a tight-knit group, I would say the DBs, but there's also a ton of competition in the group as well. Do you feel like that's what makes you guys better is that you compete with each other, but you're also trying to help each other? >> I most definitely, there's no there's no hate in the room. It's all love, we do everything out of love and we compete on the field, but we come out and you see the guys we're talking to each other, we're asking each other questions and or asking how can we get better, what did we see when when one person is on the field and other people off the field, so we're always just trying to find like little nuggets here and get ourselves better, but also help everybody else get better as well. >> Do you like the challenge of being both the the nickel and the dime in this off and defensive scheme? >> Oh, most definitely. Um I just feel like I just show the confidence that the D-staff have in me to, you know, go out there and be able to play multiple positions at a high level. And um it just give myself a lot of I don't know, like characteristics on the field like I can go do a lot of things and like I love playing like that cuz you don't know what I'm doing, so I'm able to disguise in so many different ways. It just open up my game to another level. >> You're having Anthony Campanile back and this defensive staff back and the relief that you all must have had knowing that you you don't have to change up the book for the first time in your NFL career. >> Facts. >> Were you a little nervous when Camp started getting all those head coaching interviews? >> Yeah, cuz you know, that's the that's how the game go for coaches and once you have a great, you know, season, um you know, other organizations are looking for a new head coach and we knew he was going to be a high candidate for that position. So, we was a little nervous, but at the same time we would have been happy for him at the same time cuz he deserve it. He's a great coach and whatever organization that would have got him would have been blessed. But, um we're happy to have him back and felt like you said, for the first time in my career, um I had the same defense DC in a long time since I don't remember when, but it's a blessing. I'm happy and all the guys here are happy. We all called each other when it happened. We was like, "Yes, please. Thank you." So, it was a good thing for us. So. >> How do you improve from the safety room? You guys had the second best takeaways, I think, in the NFL. How do you improve to get be the team at the top for the safety room? >> Just continue to do what we did last year. Don't get complacent. Just take every day as an opportunity and we just work hard. I feel like that's what we did last year and we don't change anything. We going for the number one spot this year, so I would just feel like the guys and and it's a little different too. Like I said, like we understand what we're looking at now and we know how to play with it. So, I feel like it's going to be a lot more plays that we could have made last year that we're going to make this year.
