title: Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza, Aidan O'Connell and Mike McCoy Presser - 6.9.26
text: Are you ready to roll? >> So, how's it how's it feel being here and how long did it take getting used to these colors after uh some of your other stops in the division? >> Well, I'm grateful for the opportunity that Clint gave me to came to come and join his staff uh and work for such a great organization. Um it starts with Mark Davis at the top obviously and uh just being a Raider is something special. uh you know obviously been in the division a couple other places and uh I know what it means to play against this organization uh to be in this division uh but it's just an honor and privilege uh to be a Raider. >> How would you describe what your dayto-day is as as basically as Clint's right-hand man and as he's taken on this for the first time and you've been a head coach? >> Yeah. Well, I was very fortunate in San Diego in 2013 uh to have Ken Wizenh Hunt on my staff and so it was great to have a guy that's been in your role. Um and like Clint and I have talked a number of times, there's so many things that come across your desk and sometimes you go, I've got to do that or I've got to answer that question. I mean, yeah, you're the head coach and you've got you've got to answer all those things. So, um you know, I I love helping him uh every day. Um it's always something different. Uh but I'm here for him and uh help him lead and um get the team prepared week in and week out regardless what the situation is. >> A lot of young coaches are nervous about having people around them who will push back, who will be that voice. Clint embraces it and loves it. What's that say about his character? >> Well, all Clint wants to do is help this organization win, and that's his number one focus. So, uh, he put an unbelievable staff together. Um, and he brought guys in that are going to help him. And I think one of the things, you know, I think as a head coach is you want to bring people in, uh, that can make maybe a weakness a strength and certain things, guys in certain roles, uh, whether it's in the offensive staff, the defensive staff, special teams, uh, my role, certain things that can really help him, uh, you know, turn this thing around and get the get us to a winning tradition, get it back. Um, and then that's what it's all about. But, you know, he has a passion for this game. He truly loves doing what he does. Comes to work every day. Uh he's a great leader and I think you can see that by the way our players are out there practicing on daily base. They've done a phenomenal job this offseason. I think it it starts with Clint's leadership and what the message is and on how he wants us to play, how he wants us to prepare uh and what we're doing. >> Is there is there any concern uh we didn't see Nobe Dean out there on the field. Is there any concern about his absence? >> One more time, please. >> The Kobe Dean. We didn't see him out there on the field today. Is there any concern with the amongst the team with his with his absence? >> No, there's no concern. He's a pro. Um, this is the off seasonason. You know, the number one thing is that we're taking it one day at a time and, you know, you get through this next couple days of the mini camp, then you get through training camp. The key thing is to have everybody as fresh as possible and ready to go for the opener. That's the number one focus. >> Before accepting this role, what gave you confidence that you and coach Kubiaak would have a similar vision? one more time. you confidence that you and coach Kubak would have a similar vision? >> Well, I was I was coached by his father um back in 1995 uh with the Broncos. Um and just understanding and knowing the type of coach uh Gary was and having played against Gary a number of years, different places. Uh then I was fortunate enough to work uh with Clint in Denver for a year. Uh and I gave him a big responsibility there. Um, I leaned on him for a number of different things when I was the offensive coordinator there and I I he has, like I said earlier, he has a passion for the game and his work ethic is unbelievable. Um, and so we've talked over the years. Um, we haven't been on a staff together since those days, but um, I I was very, you know, my family and I, my wife and I, my kids, we were very excited, uh, to be a part of the Raiders organization and work for Clint and be able to help him in any ways. just knowing the success he's had, uh, the type of coach he is, the type of person he is, the family man he is, uh, it's just it's an honor to help him. >> Coach Qers, Red Nation Radio 920, going back to Nico, just wanted a clarification. Is he in the building working or is he? >> Yeah, he's been here. >> Okay. You obvious obviously speak very highly of Clint and you saw him give him responsibility when you're with him before. How early could you tell like, oh, this, you know, he's something and maybe he could reach this level, >> right? right when I the first when we first started doing things together um and just understanding you know the questions he asked and that that was a great thing as a young coach in his role in Denver. He he was never he never hesitated to come my office and ask a question about, you know, a quarterback progression or or why we run it. Why do we call it this way, uh, protection rules, things like that. And that's what you want. You want the young coaches to be able to speak up and don't hold back anything. Uh, and he he asked all the right questions at the right time. They may not be in the middle of a meeting or something, but he'd wait and he'd come to my office and sit down and say, "Okay, hey, why are you calling this or what is the progression or what would you tell the quarterback in this situation?" Um, and things like that. What have you seen from this? You obviously been around a lot of quarterbacks, your time, coach, a lot of quarterbacks. What have you seen from this quarterback room in particular, uh, maybe excites you? >> Well, I love the way they work together. Um, you know, we left the building last night, whatever time that was, and uh, you know, as I walked through the dining area down there, a bunch of them were sitting down, the quarterbacks, some other players were just sitting there having dinner together, hanging out, and we kind of all walked out at the same time. But you you just love the way they work together. you know, there's only one quarterback who's going to be playing and that'll play itself out over training camp and how things go, but they just they work together and they help each other out. Uh, you know, the two younger guys are very fortunate to have the two vets in front of them to see every day, you know, what it means to be a pro, how they work. And everyone's different. Everyone prepares different, everyone has different throwing styles, things like that. But you just love to see the relationship and the connection that they've built and the unselfishness of each one of them helping each other. uh because as a young quarterback uh there's a lot to learn and that we got two vets uh that have done an outstanding job helping the young guys and that's what it's all about. We've got a the character in this building is out of this world. the vets and we got a young team so we got to help a young a lot of these younger players but the leaders have really stepped up to help the young guys show them the way >> when there's a regime change you know there's just some time with fluidity guys learning where to be right places where coaches want them there seem to be none of that just extremely efficient very fluid what does that say about what are you guys doing because I've been doing this for few decades and that's not normal to see it as efficient as it is right now >> we'll give coach all the credit in the world um for establishing a standard that's very high. Um he's very demanding. Uh he's not going to hold back on anybody. You know, in the meetings, team meetings, he's not afraid to point anybody out at practice. It doesn't matter who you are. He's going to coach you hard. Uh there's a standard and that's the standard he set. And you know, if if you want to be great in this league, there's a way to prepare, a way to practice, uh a way to work, a way to to be connected as a team. the things we've done uh it's been outstanding. But it's everything starts uh with Clint's leadership and the way he treats the players. >> There is a lot of experience and innovation in that offensive room, coaching room. You have a young quarterback in Fernando Mendoza and when it comes to his development, which is extremely important around here obviously. >> Um how do you guys go about sort of streamlining that so that it's kind of a one voice to him so it doesn't overwhelm him with all the ideas that are in that building? Well, the great thing about Fernando is and I I go back to uh one of the first times I met him or the first even go back to the combine uh when you have the interviews and things like that. You don't have a lot of time at the combine, but is the question that he asked. He wants to know why and and that's the great thing and I think Andrew and the rest of the offensive staff have done a great job because the first year is a challenge not just for rookies but for everybody. there's so much information and you're trying to, you know, you're installing a system for the long haul. It's not just this year, but it's for the future and and it changes from year to year. Don't get me wrong there. You're always adjusting to your players and what they do best. Uh but the great thing about it is just the way the coaches have decided, okay, we're going to have this these six installs. This is how we're going to install it. We're going to repeat it a number of times through the offseason program. They're going to come back to training camp. It's back to day one install again. Uh but the most important thing is to explain to these players this is why we do it this way. This is why the foot works. Um you know this is why we have a certain step you know fivestep drop, sevenst step drop, quick passing game, all those different things. Here's the protection rules and really explain to all the players this is why we're doing things. >> You have a a wide variance between experience Kirk and then Fernando. where's the starting point for you guys or just the fine line of you know Kirk kind of been here done that whereas Fernando is just starting so getting that message across to both quarterbacks in a way that is not wasting somebody's time but also being beneficial to the young guy. >> Well, this is the first year in the system and obviously uh some of the coaches have been with Kirk before so they know more about him than the other guys. But the most important thing is that we teach the system number one and then find out what our players do best. Not just the quarterbacks. Obviously, it's built around a quarterback and you have a system in place. Uh but you got to look at everybody on this roster and say, "Okay, offensively, what do we do best and what do the quarterbacks like?" And you know, there's going to be a time once we get through this and get closer to games where you get to the, you know, you start game planning. You start asking the quarterbacks, you know, what are their favorite plays? What do you really like? What do you not like? You know, I'm a firm believer in that red pen is your best friend. If you don't like something, cross that out. We got plenty other calls. You know, as coaches, we got too many plays in a game plan more often than not. So, uh, but it's all about the players and finding out what they do best. >> You talk about Fernando asking the right questions. It's one of the first things about what just since he's been in the building, what have you seen just about him embracing this this opportunity? >> Well, you just the you love the type of person he is. Um, his leadership, you know, the way he is with his teammates. You know, you see, like I mentioned earlier, the guys having dinner last night. You see the way he interacts with everybody, the way he is in the huddle. Um the way he is, you know, in between, you know, his reps of talking to guys. Uh he's a leader and he's got a very bright future. Uh he understands the challenge at hand of, you know, what he has to do uh to become a pro and learn. And I can't say enough about, you know, the coaches um in the quarterback room and then the the vets that are here helping him and then the other teammates, you know, that are are helping him uh learn how to be a pro and what it's about uh playing in the NFL. >> You've seen a lot of quarterback rooms, but how rare is it to find a veteran and rookie who are genuinely interested in making each other better? It's great to see um it says a lot about the character of the guys in the room. It's when you see people that want to help each other and they understand. You know, Kirk's played a long time. He's played a long time. He's been in a lot of different rooms. You know, Aiden has done a phenomenal job from the day we signed Kirk to the day we draft Fernando. He hasn't changed at all. And it just says so much about those type of players. And it's special as coaches when you get those type of people in a building and they're unselfish and they want to help each other. Um because they understand the business. It is a business and they understand that. But they're doing everything they can to help the younger players. >> You were you were just in Tennessee where Cam started from from day one. I think you were in Denver when you ease Timbo into that role. Can you talk about the advantages and benefits of kind of both situations with a first round quarterback starting from day one and also kind of learning under a veteran? >> Well, then I then I also had Trevor Lawrence in Jacksonville. That was a second year, but it was a second system. >> Um, so it's just it's it's not going to happen overnight. Just learning and mastering everything. There's going to be mistakes, but I'm I'm a true believer in the only way to learn is by making some mistakes. And there's the ups and the down. It's a long season. Um, you know, Tim, we just did a special, we're going to have, we did some work on him the other day for a special the NFL is going to put out here. Uh, you know, in 2010, we drafted him at the 25th pick and Kyle Orton was the starter and, uh, he came in at the end of the year and then the next year in 2011, John Fox was the head coach and, you know, middle of the season. We made a change. We were down against San Diego and Tim comes in and almost leads us to a victory. Throws a hail Mary, which we had a good opportunity to catch. We did not. And then the rest is history with Tim and what he did there. And um so it's just it takes time and everybody's different. You know, Trevor got on a roll there early that his second year. We kind of struggled a little bit early on just learning the system and we were trying to find out and that's on us as coaches also of what he does best and you know don't try to do too much and then all of a sudden he got hot you know then we had the playoff run. We had the big win against the Chargers things like that. Um so everybody's different. Cam, you know, he had his ups and downs early and then he was so efficient at the end of the year. Unfortunately, he got hurt the last game of the season in Jacksonville, you know, after he scored the touchdown the first game. But if if you watch all three of those guys, you can see the growth over time and there is the frustrations at times that, you know, they don't make a play and and they've always been it's been easy for them and they hit a little bit of a wall at times. You say just keep going. You're going to learn. You got a very very bright future. But it's hard. the game, the tempo, the speed of the game from the preeason to the regular season, you get into the playoff, how the tempo just picks up and it's it's a kind, you're always learning. >> Is is teaching a young quarterback like Fernando, you mentioned just mistakes learning. Okay, the windows here are not the windows at Indiana. The speed here is is that just more is caught than taught on the book? Well, I think the great thing, the way Clint, Andrew, um, and the entire offensive staff are teaching this offense to the offense about the anticipation, the footwork, you know, if it's one hitch, if it's two hits, where you're going with the ball. Uh, and then they're sticklers on it. They are on it every single play. They're always talking about the mechanics of everything. Uh but I think the biggest adjustment or one of the biggest adjustments besides the speed is just the anticipation you have to play with at this level because what is open in this league it's you got to understand that it a tight window that's open and you got to anticipate and uh the ball placement and certain things. Um, you see, you know, Aiden's a great example down there in Kirk. You look at it also like in the red area, you know, the way you throw the ball on the goal line versus the back end line. It's been good. >> Let's wrap it up with Sam and Ryan. >> Have you uh have you had Fernando watch any 90s movies like you were doing with with Mike in Atlanta? >> No, I don't think so yet. Um, occasionally things will come up, uh, you know, talking to, hey, have you seen this movie? You seen that movie? Um, so we kind of get an understanding of culturally where our lives intersect and where they don't. I brought up heavyweights today at practice. I said, uh, you see heavyweights and most of the coaches had, but uh, my teammates my teammates had not, so I I understand where my generation is is fitting there, but uh, uh, I did get some laughs out of the coaches, so that was good. I was wondering how similar or different is Clint Kubak the head coach compared to Clint Kubak the offensive coordinator your position coach back when he was in Minnesota. >> I like that question. Um I may have to tread lightly with the answer but no he's been he's been great. Um I just think he's got there's a uh football matters to him. Um there's an intensity there. There's an attention to detail. There's an urgency, probably the best word, that I've sensed from him as a head coach, that I think is really good for our football team. But it does cause me when I'm driving into work in the morning, I'm kind of like, I feel it. I'm like, I better be on today. Like, am I like check my watch like four times to make sure I'm I'm on time or early because I just feel like he brings that sense of urgency that the great coaches tend to bring, right? And um it's certainly not a laid-back atmosphere. I'll just say that. And I think that's a positive, but um I think that comes too with being a head coach. You know, you feel that weight as a head coach and and um it's not an easy position to sit in. It can be lonely at the top. And I I think he um he also then, you know, as the head coach has to has to make sure that we're running a tight ship and that we're a great operation. And I think we all feel that urgency. I mean, pre-practice in the locker room, people feel that. And I think that can be a healthy thing, right? It can bring out the best in us. But um you know, the last two months, it's not a picnic. you know, we're not out here just kind of having fun. Like it's it's work and you feel that in the locker room pre-practice the way guys mindset is and just guys are really focused or going over their stuff two or three times because they don't want to be the guy who made the mental error. So, um I think that's a really positive thing, but it's not a country club. >> Can you see yourself as a coach? >> I like to sleep and I like to I like to have a social life. So, I probably don't. I was saying that I could coach if I could hire all my buddies. Like all the guys that I played with, all the guys that I'd love to hang with, I could sit with them all day and coach. But, uh, who knows? Maybe I love football. I want to be around the game in some way, shape, or form. I just don't know if that's, you know, coaching popcorn or football with my boys or if it's broadcasting or coaching football at a high level, but I want to be around the game for sure. >> Awesome. >> How you guys doing? Laurian, have you seen it go? >> Uh, I plan on seeing it this weekend. Plan on seeing this weekend. Well, we we'll finish our mandatory mini camp, so a little bit more time off. Vets will be off and the the foot will still be on the gas pedal, but have have an extra day, so it'll be good time to go watch it. >> Uh Kirk was just talking about sticking to the movies. He's talked about how like you guys like to share movies and what you watch and haven't watched. I was wondering what movies have he put you on so far. >> Yeah, Kirk, you know, he's a great guys. Put me on a bunch of oldies for sure. But uh No, I'm I'm joking. He's uh Kirk Kirk has a great movie taste. We actually went the other day to go watch the movie Pressure, World War II movie. I didn't think I was going to like it, but it was actually a really enjoyable movie and it was a fun time. >> What's been, you know, the most challenging part just early on in in this journey in in the NFL? And is there even an intimidation factor you have to get over early on or no such thing? Well, I think there's always a transition, especially from the college level to the NFL level, and it's having those positive stressors and that growing period, and there's going to be some growing pains. And luckily, I feel confident that I'm able to see the field well and that my growing pains are coming from, hey, I got to time up my footwork a little better with the routes and intricacies here and there. And I'm really working hard with the coaching staff who's pushing me and have done a phenomenal job of relaying and communicating the information needed. And it's up to me to take full advantage of that. And I feel like I've been growing every day from the first day of OTAAS. Then today mini camp, I feel like I'm leaps and bounds ahead of where I was. >> You went through a similar situation going from Cal to Indiana and you had to learn it in a hurry. Yes. with some high expectations at Indiana and it didn't necessarily always start off well, but it got better and it got better and it got better. How much can that benefit you in this transition? Yeah, I think having that experience of coming from Cal to then go to Indiana and honestly having a really rough spring in Indiana of learning there's a big learning curve to now which is I want to say which now you know with more experience and having dealt with that transition already it has been smoother in the fact of learning new offense getting new information learning new teammates receivers offensive linemen and being able to take that experience and have a neutral mindset of where, hey, I'm learning. I'm growing. This isn't the Super Bowl today. This day, I'm trying to become the best version of myself so I can best serve my teammates down the road. >> How do you b balance the kind of all the fan pair being the top pick and all the things like you know, you did the thing at the Knights game the other night and everything like that? All all that stuff with the fact that you have all this stuff on your plate and trying to speed up the learning curve. >> Yeah, congratulations to the Knights. I thought the Knights game was a great opportunity to get some off the- field team bonding. Was able to go with some of the offensive linemen and Connor Hayward the fullback. So, not saying he's offensive lineman, he's, you know, fullback. And so, so that was a good experience itself, but from the outside in, there's no denying it. There is fanfare and there is excitement. And I just try to do that by control the controllables because expectations are all in the future tense. And if I just focus on the present tense, I know that I will be able to, you know, get there one day in the future. But worrying about the future is not going to do me any good right now. So, I'm just trying to work every single day. And right now, I'm repping with the threes and a little bit with the twos. So, right now, I'm just trying to prove myself and do the best in whatever rep I get and treat every single rep like it is a Super Bowl. >> Lot of youth on this team. Can you talk about the youth on this team, please? >> Yeah. No. Yeah. There there's a lot of youth on this team and I haven't had much experience being on other NFL teams, but I believe the team is very connected and it's a young core. It's a young core, so we're all able to mesh together and we're all learning and growing together. >> Aiden and Kirk told us that it's been a very collaborative group. You guys are all kind of balancing off one each other. How has that helped you so far when it comes to your own learning process? >> Yeah, I feel like we're all in different stages. Kirk being more veteran, Aiden being in his fourth year or fifth, pretty sure it's fourth, and then me being in my first year, and then also Jacob Clark, the other uh UDFA quarterback who's also in his first year. We've all come together and have combined our experiences, whether it's from an experienced mind, a naive mind, and Aiden's mind who's a little bit of, you know, who's a mix, who's a little bit of veteran. And to be able to collaborate with Jano, coach Janokco and coach Sullivan and coach Kubak has been very very influencing for me in my development. Whether it's just sitting back and listening to Kirk have a conversation with coach Denoko, whether it's asking Aiden Okonnell a question, whether it's hearing coach Kubak to the whole talk to the whole offense. It's been an overload of information and I've been trying my best to take on all the information and try to apply it on the field. Coach McCoy said the only way for rookies to learn is through mistakes. Is there a mistake that you've made yet that you had to go through to truly learn it? >> Yeah, there there are mistakes I've made in practice for sure. Like everybody makes mistakes, but there are mistakes I've made in practice and a little bit of after practice. I'm a little frustrated I made that mistake, but it's good and it's healthy because when you're frustrated about it, you're put more focus and intent on not making that mistake again. And like the coaches say, there's no problem making a mistake, but you don't want to be a repeat offender. So with that, I'm just doing my best not to play tense so I don't have any mistakes because then you will consequently have mistakes, but more of really dialing in, reading my notes every single night, seeing the common themes and common trends, trying to work on those common technique, themes and trends, and then apply them over the weekend. So then they show up in team period whether it's seven on seven team to minute in a flow state where I'm not needing to focus on hey don't do this don't do this because then you're going to end up doing that. >> Mike uh when he came in and also Kirk and Aiden all said one of the most impressive things about you is the questions that you ask the willing willingness to ask the questions and to learn from them. I guess how important is that to you to to be you know willing to ask those questions and to try to learn from whatever you need to and you know express like hey I don't know this like how could I get better at this? >> I think that really stems from the support of the quarterback room coming from the coaches and the other quarterbacks from day one voicing that I should ask questions if I have any hiccups or if I have any inconsistencies about any concepts. Hey Fernando, ask a question. We we won't ever think this, you know, ask questions, ask questions. So that has developed my flexibility in meetings to ask questions, which I really applaud them for allowing me to do that. And it's helped me a ton. And it's not only about asking questions. It's um and most of it is actually listening is listening to the conversations, taking it in and listening to the end of the conversation. And then sometimes at the end of the meeting when your question wasn't answered, then deploy that. I know you're going to put a hit the pause button here in a couple of days, which is probably going to be beneficial after going every through everything that you've gone through for this past year, but do you have a game plan in place to to make sure that um that's still a productive time even when you're as as you're right to kind of take a little bit of a break here? Yeah, I believe the rookies are staying here until June 23rd, but even in the July break, looking forward to spending time in Las Vegas as well and have making that game plan with Alex Guerrero, with the coaching staff and with the training staff in order to maximize my development and my development and what needs to happen before training camp. And that's not saying, "Hey, every single day we're gonna work from 6 am to 6 pm." But it's saying, "Hey, you can have maybe these days off, but let's maximize the themes that you need to get ready before training camp, before the first preseason game, and let's have a game plan and action so we're not just feeling motivated one day and the other day. Like, let's have a game plan in action." So, we're we're dialing that all in. But right now, we're mini camp, mini camp, mini camp. And then after that, before everybody heads out of town, we will convey that. All right, last one here. Levi. >> Oh, most recently you were just named to the top 100, you know, most influential people in sports list. I'm not sure if you I'm not sure if you just learned >> I appreciate telling me. >> But yeah, no. Uh, you and your college coach, uh, Kirk, you're both on the list. So, I guess now that you do know, you know, how cool is it to, you know, be on that list with guys like LeBron and Saquon and people of that nature? >> Yeah, it's a blessing. It's a blessing. And it really comes from having a great team and great teammates and and great coaches of that of of my past year in college because without them then we wouldn't have you know won as many games as we did and without that you're not on the list. So, it's all it's all a trickle effect. And I think I'm I'm happy that I'm back down on the bottom of the totem pole because although it's great to get some reminders from the college career and appreciate you telling me that, it's good to start back from stage one from level one having worked my way back up and get a get a sense of industriousness to be successful at the next level. But again, it is a huge blessing. Time from what I've always seen is a great magazine. always very intriguing and a list with legends like LeBron James like so many others. It's very it's an incredible honor. >> Thanks guys. Congratulations on the graduation. Thank you guys. Sorry guys. God bless.

title: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen speaks ahead of veterans minicamp
text: Um obviously excited to start uh mini camp this week. Um we've had a good off seasonason so far. Want to continue that this week and finish strong. Um as far as practice is concerned, uh Daniel will still be on the same deal. He'll do individual and seven on seven. Uh Buck and AP will not participate. Um get them ready to go for training camp. Um, so that communication at that spot is critical and we're getting a lot of reps, you know, in that right now. And, you know, that'll continue into training camp. but been pleased with where he's at right now >> with how to say >> yeah I I mean I'm not going to put a timet on it but at some point in training camp whether it's the start or maybe a couple weeks in you know we're just going to be smart with him too make sure he's ready to go >> still on schedule >> yeah very happy with his progress I mean he's hitting all his landmarks um each and every week every day putting in the work um but he's feeling good you know it's like I said it's good to get him out there last week in seven on seven do it again this Um, then I know he'll work tirelessly this summer, you know, to be ready for training camp. >> Has anything surprised you about his progress? Like, is he progressing faster than you thought or or anything like that? >> Um, you know, you kind of look at the history of Achilles injuries and I know some guys heal faster than others, but you know, 6 months out there running around with the guys um is pretty impressive. You know, I think some of these injuries, you know, eight, nine months right in there and he's kind of on track, maybe a little bit ahead of schedule. Um, so very pleased with that. >> I know you're looking forward to getting, you know, some key guys back on defense this year, but you also have had a lot of turnover on that side of the ball. How how can you tell how it's coming together? >> Well, I think just the camaraderie and the chemistry, guys communicating on the field right now. Obviously, not in pads, but uh just the communication piece, making sure the guys are on the same page. And I think that's got to continue into training camp and make sure we're all on the same page uh when week come week one comes around. Um, they got to understand our systems and how we operate within the systems, you know, to be out there to go make plays because if you don't know what to do, it's going to be hard to go make plays. >> Riley, >> uh, not right now. I mean, both of those guys are having a good offseason. Um, they're both doing some really good things and it's back and forth right now. Um, and so we'll see where that goes. >> Yeah, as of right now. Yeah. How do you evalate that you guys have brought in? >> Yeah, I think that's a great question. I think there is that's going to be an open competition. Obviously, Dulan's been here. Um, he's taking a lot of reps right now, but you know, we got Treadwell and we signed Westbrook, who's a good player that's playing in this league for a while. Um, so we'll see how camp goes, but I'm excited for that battle, you know, there. I think the biggest thing is consistency like who's going to be the most consistent there um day in and day out playing and play out um to go help us win games. >> How would you describe his overall career art first round pick a find a way to? >> Yeah, I would say really proud of his growth and development. I mean, he's a former first round draft pick that's kind of been through it a little bit. Um, but he's been here for a couple years, been on the practice squad, but really grown up. Just a true veteran, um, that understands it, that does anything that's asked of him, understands his role on this football team, and now he's got a opportunity to go compete, uh, to go get some good playing time. So, um, I'm really excited for him and his opportunity. What have you seen from? >> Yeah, I think there's growth. I think understanding the system going into year two is a part of it. And I think you will see, you know, a lot of the growth, you know, going into training camp when the pads come on because it's it is hard to look at running backs with no pads on, but you can still see a little bit of the vision and the cuts and stuff, but the physicality when the pads come on is going to be a big deal. >> What did you like most? >> Yeah, you know what? He's kind of a glider runner, good slasher, stretch cut guy. Um, you know, that's that is a physical runner. You saw a little bit of that in training camp obviously last year and the reps that he got, you know, late in the season against Houston. Um, so I'm excited for his growth and his development um, as a runner, as a pass protector is going to be big going into year two. Obviously, there's a lot of exotic blisses that you got to pick up in this league and um, you know, taking the next step in his growth process in that stuff. is that you got >> Yeah, it's a huge part of it. I mean, third downs in this league, you got a whole bunch of stuff coming at you that you got to be prepared for and you prep for each and every week. Um, but obviously the back's got to be a huge part of that, you know, and protection. >> How is having Daniel back in year two, I realiz all that? >> Yeah. >> Having that having him back, how does that allow the offense to kind of grow in year two? >> Yeah, I think it's going to grow tremendously. just the communication, certain things we can do with the line of scrimmage. I mean, he did a lot of it last year. Um, but there's been a lot of great communication this off season. I mean, we just had a walk through out there. Just different looks we were getting, trying out different things, him checking plays, uh, protection stuff. I mean, it's pretty impressive to see. So, I'm really excited for that process, you know, going into training camp and this season. This is this is very hypothetical, but um as he's coming back, I mean, he'll be ready, right? But like how mobile you are, how exposed you can be, we'll see. >> Do you think as a play caller you have to consider some of that what you're asking him to do? >> Well, I think it depends on how he's feeling. title: DeMeco Ryans Texans Minicamp Media Availability | Full Q&A
text: All right. Fire away. You got nothing. All right. I'm about ready to roll. Just did. You're good. I can hear you. I can hear you. >> So, I know we've done this a bit. I don't know how much to say about the shorts, but OTAs and then the break. I always wonder, what do you How do you advise a team in this time between mini camp and training camp? >> The advice during the break for for me it's always making sure you get some time to truly get some rest, get some relaxation, but also at the same time you still have to continue to work with the gains that you built, the you know, the conditioning that you've built up throughout the OTAs, throughout the veteran mini camp. You still want to see guys continuing to work for at least 2 or 3 weeks and then give themselves a little break and then we got to ramp it up again and get ready to roll because as we know come training camp for us in Houston it's a little different. We have to be You have to be built different to play here in Houston when you deal with the humidity, deal with the heat that we have to go through. So, we want our guys They truly have to come back and begin working out in Houston at least 3 weeks before camp so they're ready to roll and be able to really thrive in camp and not just try to survive. >> You've been a part of the Texans for a few years backing up O'Neal and Will. What is filling that void in his absence? What does it look like and who are some guys that you'll call upon to to replace him? >> We're excited about the D-line that we have. We'll continue to roll our guys as much as possible. That's how how we operate. So, we really want eight, nine guys who can go out there and play in the rotation. We're still figuring out who that eight or nine guys will be. It'll be really tough competition in training camp that I'm excited to see. Excited to really see our young guys in the interior, see how they perform in camp. >> Speaking of Sheldon, uh we got a chance to see Sheldon Rankins back out there today. Last year, um you and Matt kind of alluded to having when he's on the field, he's like a uh another defensive coach for you all. What is it going to be like having him around and being able to uh help the process of bringing Kaden McDonald along? >> Sheldon brings a a calming presence to the defense. We do a lot of communication. We put a lot on those guys from a a standpoint of talking to each other, linebackers talking to the defensive line. So, when you have a guy of Sheldon's caliber who's seen it all, done it all, very smart guy, very aware of formations, he can ID things that a lot of young guys can't do and we don't ask them to do. But, we can put more on Sheldon's plate because of his experience. And having him there with Kaden is going to be I think significant for Kaden and his development. Kaden should grab a hold of Sheldon and not and not let him leave without gaining some type of insight, some type of knowledge, you know, every day on what it's like to play at one of the toughest positions in football, interior defensive line. He needs to learn that from a guy who's done it for over 10 years. >> Has his leadership shown with the fact that we see what what he was able to do with Will with his rookie year and what Will Will has grown into being able to take those things from Sheldon. Is that the same thing for Kaden? >> Sheldon poured a lot into Will and you see Will now benefiting from that, but Will is also taking it and he's pouring into the younger guys himself. And that's what the NFL has always been built on. I had veteran guys, Marlon Greenwood, Sean Barber, Danny Clark, guys who poured into me. And that's the only way I knew how it should be done. And when I went through my career, it was my chance to pour into guys like Zach Dials, Brian Cushing, Jordan Hicks, Mychal Kendricks. That's what the league is built on. >> When it comes to Ariante Ervin, last year he was a rookie. Like all rookies, you go through the growing pains at the start. You get better as the year goes on. What do you see from him, what he's done this off-season, the work he's put in, and what do you expect from him this fall? And a quick follow-up. >> Tay has done a really great job of preparing himself this off-season. Uh year two for him, he's definitely hitting in the weight room pretty hard. He's He's He's playing He's looking more stronger. He's playing aggressive. He's smart knowing where he needs to be. It's not new to him, so you can see a guy who's really He's calm in what he's asked to do. He's calm with the position and things that we're asking him to do. He's doing a really good job of >> Coach, can you make sure what you like about where the team is at at this stage of the off-season? How do you feel about just the quality of the team overall? That you got to kneel, you got everybody all together once. Thank you. >> Our team is is looking great. I feel really really good about where we are as a team. It's one of the best OTAs that we've had since I've been here in the past four I'm really excited about training camp. I can't You know, really excited to see these guys actually put on pads and see who shows up in the pads. Like it's it's one thing in the shorts. Some guys can make plays in shorts, but you put the pads on and play real football, you see who can really show up. But our guys have shown up. Everything that I've asked them to do, they've shown up with the right mindset. They've worked the right way. And so I We have a lot a really great group of guys, and I think we're going to build a really great team this year. >> You guys um You mentioned that this is the best best yeah, this way the off-season since you've been here. There's a lot of time invested on the line. Team wins, you lose, you guys all have to do things to see both sides of this last season. How much does that equate to just how verbal and vocal guys are to where how have a lot of veterans where it's even kind of certain to be a better better you can build on a small minded team. >> When I first came here in 2023, it was really to establish a mindset and an identity of who I wanted the Texans to be. And as we've seen over the past 3 years, we have that identity. We play ball aggressive, we play physical, we do it the right way. Like we're we're going to be the toughest team to suit up every time we suit up, right? That's the guys that we bring in, that's the culture that we built. Now, I don't have to go back and reestablish our identity and how we play. You know, as we grow as a team, as I've grown as a head coach, for me, it's more so now about how much how much smarter can we play as a team? Like how can we be more elite on our execution? Our communication, can it be louder? Can we echo it more? Can we truly be tied together every time we line up? And that's what I've seen when I talk about, you know, the process of us this year being better, I've seen better communication. I've seen guys just being able to absorb more defense, absorb more offense, formations, motions. Guys are just able to handle more because, you know, it's second year in our offense, fourth year in our defense. That's you know, it's a given, but it's also the veterans that we have, the leaders that we have at each and every position allows me to see it, step back as a head coach to see, wait, we just need to keep fine-tuning. Fine-tuning, fine-tuning of the details, not necessarily every period is a competitive get-after-it period. It's more of a mental check, and that's what we're working on this offseason and we'll continue to develop that in the training camp. >> So, you So, you talked about So, you talked about Jamal Hill earlier in the practice. I'm curious about that group, the linebacker group. Just what can you tell us about it? >> The linebacker group is is is a really competitive room. Probably the most competitive it's been in a while. We have a lot of young players, which I like. A lot of young players in that room that can they can all play. That's the exciting part about it. A lot of great athletes in that position. Jamal is one of those guys. He's He's shined and flashed a couple plays on special teams for us last year. I remember play versus the Cardinals. Our one of our special teams goals was to go take the football away. And Jamal goes down first play kickoff, first play of the game, and he puts his hat on the football. We get a huge turnover. He really set the tone for us. And just still pouring into him right to not only get it done on the special teams aspect, but also grow as a player to where man, you can you go out and play right? True first, second, third down for us. And he's growing. He's He's gotten better being a safety who's converted to the linebacker position. He's done a a really good job of that. So, the more I can pour into those guys that's I'm always close to those linebackers. Those are my babies. So, I love working with the linebackers. And they're they're a fun group. They're really really smart group. That's I would say because Billy Davis done an outstanding job of working with those guys to get them caught up to speed. Our rookies are probably some of the smartest rookies that I've I've had the chance to work with. So, that's encouraging to me. >> We'll take a few more. >> It's not often you get an opportunity to spend time with somebody you played with in the league. When you had Texas State football coach GJ here today, what's some of the things you talked about? Just catching up? Did you get an opportunity to see practice? What was that like for you guys? >> It was fun seeing GJ come out to practice today. See just congratulating him on the growth that he's had in his career as a head coach at Incarnate Word, moving on to Texas State, taking that program to bowl games, first-ever bowl games in their past 3 years. So, he's done a great job of, you know, establishing a culture there at Texas State, and I'm proud of the success that he had, former former uh teammate there in Philly with him, also uh uh former neighbor of mine. So, it's always good to good to see guys that flourish after the game and still being involved, still coaching. And uh talking to G.J., you just see the passion that he has for the recruiting, for helping young men, and that's what I I love hearing that when I talk to young coaches. >> Last week, Nick talked about being able to put some more tight ends on the field, and it seems like that's a trend the NFL's starting to put together. What kind of challenges from a defensive perspective do three tight ends present, and then what kind of advantages the offense will get when they put those three tight ends on the >> Uh Kasey wants all the tight ends, all right? Put four of them out there. Now, it's uh it's the tight ends pose a a matchup problem. And it's not just because it's the tight end, it's how the the tight ends have evolved in our game. Now, you got more of pass more pass threat tight ends than we've had in the past. In 2006, hey, you put four tight ends on the field, and it's just it's goal line. You're not doing that now. Now, you have guys who are true receiving threats. So, when you have that, are you matching up in base personnel? Are you matching up in nickel dime personnel? Well, it really depends on who that tight end is. All right, and you match up accordingly. So, it's a it's a chess match when you're going against defenses and you put 13 personnel out on the field. Like, having the ability to throw the ball in personnel, those percentages have, I mean, skyrocketed over the past 10 years. So, just having that flexibility by an offensive coordinator to have tight ends that we could put out, and not just last year we put a lot of um extra old lineman packages out on the field which kind of you kind of show your hand easier when you have the extra old lineman. So now having the versatility and the depth of the group that we have now should open up a ton more options for us when it comes to being able to disguise some personnel. >> When it comes to Keelan Rutledge and getting his feet wet and transition you're seeing from him, what kind of look is he giving you and how does it feel? >> Keelan's done a great job. Keelan's moved around from from guard to center. He's done a great job with both. Really great communicator as a young player. Aggressive, intense, just like the tape you saw at Georgia Tech. So it's it's looked great so far you know in OTAs. I'm excited to see him as another guy with all the rookies. I'm just excited to see the guys put the pads on in training camp and truly compete, get the opportunity to play in some preseason games. >> How do you feel about your whole defense having to deal with or have shoulder rings? What was it like when you can kind of see you know what it looks like but to have them all out there together with some of the new additions like Blankenship and McDonald and everybody. What did it look like to you? >> Offenses are going to struggle. >> Hey coach, I just wanted to ask you about what you want from the players. What do you How hard do you think you need to kind of take a break during this time because it's such a long season. And are you planning to What do you What do you hope for yourself during the break between mini camp and >> Looking forward to a break. I I have not had a break since our last playoff game. So I've been working ever since and getting after it. So much needed break is coming. So I'm I'm excited about that being able to spend some time with family, take the kiddos to Disney World and get to enjoy that for a little bit. So it's some much needed time to just get away, really allow the mind to just reset, refresh so I come back to training camp, you know, ready to roll. All good. Thank you guys. Enjoy your break.

I feel really really good about where we are as a team. It's one of the best OTAAS that we've had since I've been here past four years. I'm really excited about training camp. I, you know, really excited to see these guys actually put on pass and see who shows up in the pass. Like it's it's one thing in the shorts. Some guys can make plays in shorts, but you put the pass and they play real football. You see who can really show up. But our guys have shown up everything that I've asked them to do. And I think we're building a really great team this year. >> You guys mentioned that this team has been at this point here. There's been a lot of time that's gone through like team walks have mental aspect. How much does that equitably? >> When I first came here in 23, it was really to establish a mindset and an identity of who I wanted the Texans to be. Like we're we're going to be the toughest team to suit up every time we suit up, right? That's the guys that we bring in. That's the culture that we built. title: Texans minicamp observations 1.0: Big day for defense, Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, Jaylin Noel
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. The Texans first day of mini camp is in the books and among the observations, obviously the defense still ahead of this offense. It's a top ranked defense from last season. And as Demo Ryan said, offenses are going to struggle against them, especially when you have the presence of Denil Hunter and Will Anderson Jr. as your bookend pass rushers. And it's a tough long day for the offensive tackles. today. That was Aranti Urser, left tackle and right tackle, primarily Trent Brown as they continue to work back Braden Smith from the neck injury I've been talking about with you guys. And hopefully Braden will be 100% at training camp. And if he has some sort of setback or if this sidelines him, then at least they have Trent Brown, a former Pro Bowl selection and the biggest offensive tackle in the NFL to step in. But going back to the defensive dominance, it does happen at times. It's something that's going to continue to happen, but it doesn't mean that the offense doesn't have their moments. So CJ Strad very good in the red zone, touchdown pass to Xavier Hutchinson. I thought his connection with Jaylen Null, it's building. We had a whole video about that, about what we're seeing from that connection and from his effectiveness in the slot. So couple notes here on practice availability. I know you guys like to know about the injury. So let me give you the updates as best I can. So Marlon Klein continues to be sidelined with a hamstring injury and that's why they were, you know, felt the need to sign Lewis Warren and cut Jaylen Wal. And they also are down another tight end, Lane Prior. Lane Prior also has a leg injury, so he's sidelined. Tank Dell, he did some drills, but not all of them. So I would call him limited. And obviously, he's still, you know, on track for training camp. That's what they're saying that he will be back at training camp. And of course, it'll be nearly 600 days from December of 2024 when he tore his interior cruciate ligament, dislocate his knee, tore his medial collateral ligament, his lateral collateral ligament. I think he's moving pretty well for a guy that had that devastating knee injury. It's just a matter of does he regain his full explosiveness? Is he able to take hits? And we won't have the answer to those questions until he plays in a real game. They don't hit in practice. So, we don't know. As you guys know, EJ Speed is out for the season after having a torn quadriceps tendon in addition to a partially torn quadriceps muscle. But the fully torn tendon is why he is out for the season. MJ Stewart, the safety, is still not practicing as he works his way back from his own torn quadricep tendon from last season. He was a starter, replaced CJ Gardenner Johnson, who was obviously a disruption to uh team chemistry and didn't play in the, you know, defensive scheme. Logan Hall is also limited due to a soft tissue injury and know that's been the case for a little while with Logan where uh he's still working his way back. It's not he's limping that bad. It's the same thing with Aiden Fischer. He has a sleeve on his leg. He did participate a lot more than Logan did. Jamal Hill is still coming back from wrist ligament surgery, but he practices. He just practices with a protective club and it makes it harder to catch the football, but he is practicing and he's expected to be full go by training camp. So, terms of other, you know, guys that are sidelined, it's a relatively healthy team. Uh Jake Hansen was a little bit limited. Don't know why, but I was told it's nothing serious. He was out there, but he didn't do everything. And then when you look at, you know, some of the other, you know, lineups, we'll get into all of that and some of more of my observations, but I always like to tell you guys who's not practicing because it's a very common question I get about who's not going. Okay, next question that you guys always want to know, the offensive line today. a lot of Jake Andrews with the first team offense. And I thought that Keelen Rutled, you know, working with the second team offense, didn't have his best practice in terms of snaps. Nothing fumbled, nothing really super arai, but not as accurate of a snapper as Jake Andrews on this day. Doesn't mean he's not going to win the center job. I still think he will, and he continues to make progress. But from left to right, Arandreas, your left tackle, left guard, Wyatt Teller, you can pencil them in. That's the guys. Center is a competition. Right guard of course is Ed Ingram on that big contract. And then right tackle I think when Braden Smith gets healthy if that happens then he'll take over the spot. But right now it was a case of Trent Brown. We saw a lot of combinations. But we saw, you know, I would say a pretty steady group with the first team offensive line. So without Nico Collins, a lot of throws to Jaden Higgins and Jaylen Null. And I thought that CJ Stra did miss a few throws, but overall was pretty good. I thought Davis Mills was sharp in the red zone. They weren't using running plays because they're not allowed to tackle at this stage. Obviously, it's a non-cont, so that's one of the reasons why. But I think David McGomery has looked really good catching passes. I think he's moving very well. Um I mentioned British Brooks has lost 17 lbs. Looks very very quick. Uh and of course he's a special teamer and he can play fullback and he can play tailback and he always seems to find his way onto this roster and they like him. I didn't know if you guys like fought for Would you be mad if I moved it back? >> No, you should do that every day. >> He's more comfortable on the edge. >> I'm an edge recorder. >> [laughter] >> We are live. >> Our last day. >> Yeah. >> It's been fun. >> Last day of school. >> It's not over but how since we're not going to see you for a while, how would you describe how the spring went relative to your expectations and objectives? >> Yeah, I didn't have [snorts] any expectations. Like I kind of told you guys I kind of wanted to come in open minded. Um I like the way it went. I I appreciate the coaches and how hard they've worked. We've been here I mean a lot of us since our last game ended took a week off and we're here, you know, so I appreciate all their hard work. I like the relationships that we have built with the players. I like the guys that we have on the team, the veterans, the guys we signed in free agent free agency, um the young guys that we drafted. I like the group. I like the buy-in. I like how hard they've worked. Um the relationships we've built. And I like the work that we've put in. I think it's just the very beginning. But I'm pleased I'm pleased with their attitudes and effort, which are the most important thing to me. >> What have you learned about this team so far? >> I kind of like what I just said. They're a team that has connected with each other. They're a team that's connected with the staff. They worked really hard in the classroom. They work really hard on the field. They're very coachable. And they're a fun group to be around. And I think we'll learn more when we start playing real football. I think we'll learn more as adversity hits because I think you learn a lot about people when things aren't, you know, just going easy. And there's jobs won, and there's jobs lost, and there's games won, and there's games lost. Um I think now now is an easy time, right? Everything's fresh. Everything's new. But from the attendance to the effort to the buy-in, um I really couldn't ask for anything more from this group of guys and the staff. >> We talk about evaluating players and your coaches, but how would you evaluate yourself in your first uh first off season here as a NFL coach? >> Yeah. Um I don't know if I'm ready to do that today. I think it it's it is Your question is very good cuz it's something that I have thought about. And I think that once we finish this week, I think it's very important that I kind of take a step back and just reevaluate everything since I've been here and look very closely at that. The things that I like that I did, the things that I didn't like that I did. Um but I think that will be very important for me to do. I'd be making stuff up right now and just giving you answers you want to hear or didn't want to hear. So I'm going to take some time and think through that and go [clears throat] over the staff, go over the players kind of like get head cuz it's been go, go, go. Um but that's something that I'll take some time and do soon. >> Can you tell us what you saw from Malik Willis and Quinn Ewers in this off-season program? >> Yeah, progress, comf- uh they're more comfortable within the scheme. they've taken more command of the huddle, they've taken more command when they're out there with the wide outs, um confidence. I I've seen the confidence grow and you know, even the conversation I had with Malik today walking down the hallway, you can just see you know, he's more comfortable and he understands the answers that are being provided for him on each play. And I just I I think he looks as good as he's looked since I've known him. And I would say the same about Quinn. I think Quinn's gotten better. Um and I just think Bobby and Bush and KP, I I think they've all done a really good job in that room. And it will be excited to really ramp them up when we get to training camp. >> With Daryl Baker and Storm Duck, how are they coming along and is there any reason for concern for their status to start training camp? >> Um you know, I I wish they were coming along a little bit quicker. Um but we'll have to wait and see how they are once we get going. >> What did you see when you turned on Kenneth Gainwell's tape? Um and then also how would you evaluate his his off-season program? >> I think he's taking a step forward. I think he's changed his I know he's changed his body. He's faster, he looks more like the guy that I saw on his college tape with his lateral quickness, his pass rush ability, his ability to play the run. Um just the way he's moving. And I also think that goes back to year one, lack of experience, lack of reps, lack of maybe a little bit of confidence as you're out there and I just feel like right now he he's starting to believe in himself and his abilities that we know that he has and hopefully once the pads come on, we'll see that to continue. >> As we know that today is an OTA, so it's voluntary, are you expecting everyone who is here in in mandatory mini camp, including Brewer and Brooks to be out there today? >> I expect Brewer and Brooks to be out there. Brewer and Brooks are here today. They'll be out there today. >> I know it's the end of the off-season program for the veterans. You've got the rookie development program. How How long are you keeping the rookies beyond this week? >> We'll keep them We'll keep them a little bit into next week. >> Another quick question also, we discussed the joint practices earlier. Can you shed some light on how many with the Washington one and how many with the Giants again? >> Yeah, we'll go one and one. We'll go one against Washington in Washington. We'll go one versus the Giants here. >> Can you assess the >> a fan of having two. >> Can you assess a K'Von Smith's off-season given that he's been in a little bit of an elevated role? >> Yeah, yeah. I certainly I think there's progress and we moved him around. I think he shows his versatility. I think he's done a good job with the scheme. We've just had such We haven't had many team reps to really with There's no pads on, you know? So, even when we go team and it's passes and it's drop-back pass and it's pass sets. Um I think there's been progress, but let's really evaluate him when the pads come on. I think we got to evaluate all these guys when the pads come on. I mean, you can see who can process. You can see who can take from the field out to the grass. You can see who can see things and react. Um So, those are all really important things. So, I I don't ever want to slight OTAs. I think they are important and I think people that say they're not, then I mean, that's clearly, you know, their preference, but it's like part one, but part two is going to be really important when we we actually play real football. >> We know that Brewer, Brooks, and Seiler are good team leaders. Um throughout the spring, are there just a couple of guys that you'd like to mention or could mention that you appreciated the leadership that you saw them show? >> I think all those guys that you mentioned have done a really good job. Malik's done a really nice job of, you know, having guys over his house, just like Seiler's done that, trying to get guys around. Brooks has done an unbelievable job. T-Dots hung out with the rookies. Um, I spent a lot of time in the DB room. Trader has done a really good job, really kind of helping out those rookies. And even talking to him, um, you know, through his experience, him having a little bit of help, he feels now like he can help the rookie guys out. Pat Paul, is another guy watching the O-line with Brewer. I see have, you know, a leadership role right now. Um, you know, those are just those are just some of the guys off the top of my head. >> I half I caught you saying that you're not a fan of doing more >> No, you can't >> You can't call him a cop. >> Oh, yes, I did catch you quickly saying you're not a fan of doing more than one joint practice. >> Are you a fan of doing two? >> Yes. It's more It's more different than a normal practice for us. We're going to watch >> You get to see how they respond. Corrections, adjustments. >> Yes, you get to see how they respond. >> you think I don't like the second day? >> Because it gets chippy. >> Yeah, I mean, you're just you're just inviting every everyone I've experienced on the second practice, which is what we used to do, you whatever team gets the best of the team day one, the other team comes out and tries to overdo it, and they're usually usually stuff just gets bad, and you have a higher chance for injury. I mean, a fight's a fight. If it happens, you cut it up. It It shouldn't happen in a joint practice. I got it. You're just worried about it going too far and anybody getting injured. Our job's to protect the team and to protect the players, and I think one good hard practice, cuz then the other thing is this, like when you look at blocks of practice, usually you have like a high day, a low day, and a medium day. Like those joint practices, you should maximize your reps. So, the ones might get 50 snaps, which is equivalent to we're working towards playing in a game. You can't do that 2 days in a row, or it's like playing two games, and you're going to wear these guys out. You You know what I'm saying? >> I have a quick question. Good catch. Some of the players have told us that they're going to, you know, try to take this next couple weeks to make sure whatever they've learned and keep themselves in shape and, you know, keep that going as they leading into training camp. What's your message to them in the next couple weeks of like what they should be doing? And based on, you know, making sure everybody comes back strong and ready to go once training camp starts. >> Mike, I kind of think it's just what you said. I mean, one, I think they need to take a deep breath, clear their minds a little bit, rest their bodies a little bit, but then they need to get back to work and make sure they come in in shape, ready to go. You know, the message is going to be make sure they're training outside a little bit, so when they come back the heat doesn't zap them. But a lot of them have made huge progress, right? And the worst thing that they can do is not continue to build on that progress, because say they're here right now and they go back and they don't do anything to get back here, it's going to take them all training camp. Where if they're here right now, and even if they just go to here, we can get them all the way up there. But if we take a ton of steps back, it's going to take us all training camp to get them where they are now, and we don't have time for that. I mean, the message is also pretty easy. I mean, we got some really good vets, right? And some guys that are pretty solidified in some roles, but then there's a lot I think there's 40-plus guys on 1-year deals and there's a ton of rookies, so there's a lot of guys in this roster who have a lot to prove. Um so it's going to ramp up in training camp for guys to try to win jobs so we can really evaluate them when we play football to see who's going to be out there. So, the guys that put in the work these next few weeks physically and mentally are going to have an advantage, and if I were one of those guys, I would take every advantage of that. >> Hey, if looking ahead, um I'm wondering what your training camp philosophy is because recently we've [clears throat] seen a trend where starters in training camp get their best work in those joint practices and preseason games they maybe don't play as much or do you have an idea of obviously you can change but do you have a general idea? >> in in Green Bay that's what we did, right? Our starters would take say we're practicing against the Giants. Our starters would go like 55 to 60 snaps in the joint practice and then we can't ask them to go play a whole lot in the preseason game. Maybe you give them the first quarter or the first drive to go out there. Where it's going to be a little bit different is when we get into the real football and there's guys battling for jobs, I'm not sure it's as clear cut where we're going to say these are the 22 starters that are going to get these 50 to 60 reps. So I think it's going to be a mix because I don't think we're going to be to that point yet. So I think you're going to see a mix of guys who are going to do both. >> With the Quick question for I'm sorry, just a >> No, you're good. We got We got both. >> Um >> [clears throat] >> there's a picture with you and Jimmy Johnson and he posted, you know, can you tell us a little about what that lunch was like and just, you know, being able to be out there I think was it the Big Chill? I think >> Yeah. Um you know, Dave and and Jimmy are real close and Dave was here all last week. Dave's been huge for me and my career and you know, he he said he asked me if I wanted to get together with Jimmy and just pick his brain and spend time with him and brought Solly along and and the three of us, you know, we just drove out, met him for lunch and just asked him a lot of questions and listened to him about, you know, his first go in Dallas and I mean they had a really rough first year and then he went on to win his Super Bowls and I asked him about his time here and I asked him about his time in all of his stops and any advice that he could give me going forward this year, advice with the coaches, advice with the players, advice on game day and just really picked his brain. But to have such a good resource and one of the the coaches of all time, you know, an hour and 15 minutes down the road. Getting that opportunity was really cool for me. Um, not only to learn, but just I mean, I you know, I said to my wife after, I mean, I'm I'm at lunch with Jimmy Johnson. That's pretty cool, you know? He's an unbelievable storyteller. He's got an unbelievable memory. just a great guy. And obviously one of the best ever coach. >> What's the best piece of advice that he gave you? That you What one is it that you like? >> his advice just for him, I, Sully, and Dave. >> Ask a question. >> He told me he His advice was to answer that question that [laughter] way. He knew he knew He knew He knew it was coming. He ate nachos. I don't think he got tuna on them. But, he ate nacho We all ate nachos. Have you Have you eaten there? >> Yeah, many times. >> Yeah? What do you get when you go? >> Tuna nachos. >> What do you get? >> Burger. It's a good place. >> I had a mahi sandwich. So, you should have told me I had a sandwich. >> Hour and 15 minutes. But, uh, >> It was an hour 15 minutes. It might have been less than an hour 15 minutes. Because you're just riding Key Largo like you just You're right there to the right. >> It's Key Key Largo's just >> We got You got to go. >> You got to go. >> I'm sure I've been. I'm sure I've been. >> This summer you got to go. >> Okay, I will go. >> And I want to I want to see you and Jimmy in a picture. >> That one. >> I wanted to ask you about the receiver unit. Obviously, they have chemistry to develop with with the quarterbacks. How How do you evaluate that now versus what you expect when training camp gets here? And what kind of work do you want to see them do in this in the off season? >> How do I evaluate the wide outs? >> The wide chemistry with wide outs in regards to chemistry receivers and understand >> I mean, all the wide outs right now are working with both quarterbacks and we're just rotating them all in. They're all I mean, just we just there's a lack of the numbers. So, it's not like there's one group going out with Malik and one group going out with Quinn. Those guys just rotate around so each quarterback is throwing with all of them. So, that's the best way right now for us to build the chemistry. And truthfully, in training camp, it's going to have to be the same way. Cuz if you look at say you have two racks of like four and four, I mean, you might go these receivers on the first two, take them out for two plays, and put them in the next two plays just so you don't wear them out. So, I think it's important to do so all the quarterbacks get a chance to work with those guys, right? So, that way it really doesn't matter what quarterback is going here and what quarterback's going here. You have all the wide outs working with both quarterbacks, which I do think is very important to build chemistry with both so we can properly evaluate the receivers and those quarterbacks. Make sense? >> Got you. >> All right, guys. I appreciate the uh >> Appreciate your time. Thank you. >> Appreciate the off-season. You guys have been great. Um so, have a great summer. Enjoy the big chill. And I'll see you I'll see you guys down the field. >> Thank you, guys.

Uh been understanding that since, you know, I've been in this in this uh in this league.
