So little little uh tweaks uh to my offseason workouts and stuff. Yeah. Uh kind of, but uh missed a few games last season uh with that foot injury, so it was kind of kind of added up to be the same kind of games. Uh but yeah, it's a long season. You got to make sure you're prepared for it, your body's ready for it, and you know, you're in condition for it. >> Super Bowl, did that kind of just go away instantly once it was over? Did that kind of motivate? And how did you kind of reconcile what happened there and how your your season progressed prior to that? >> Yeah, nothing like that just goes away. Uh, you know, something I sat with for, you know, a couple weeks. Uh, tried to get over it obviously, but, you know, waited a couple weeks to watch to even watch the Super Bowl, but after that, yeah, flush it. Uh, see, seeing what we did wrong, uh, seeing the things we did well and just seeing how we could get better and, you know, if we're in that situation again, how to approach it. >> What was your reaction then when you saw you're going to Seattle week one? >> Uh, we love it. Oh, we love it. little little revenge game. Uh first game of the season. It should be a good one. >> The differences for Drake just commanding the huddle from last year to this year. >> Uh yeah, just that uh he he's expecting more of us. Uh he's pushing the tempo more. There's things he's trying to get better at and we're being intentional about uh you know this spring. Uh I won't tell you everything, but yeah. Uh he's just just getting better in each facet. >> Battle for that number three running back spot. How have you seen those guys land on that responsibility? >> Yeah. Uh to be honest with you, it's spring football. Every every position is open. Nobody has a, you know, a set position. There's no ones, twos, threes right now. So, we're just all out here working hard, trying to get better. And, you know, chips fall where fall where they may. >> Thank you guys. >> Was it hot today for y'all? >> It was all right out of here in the shade. >> Oh, I'm about to say. Yeah. Um Kevin, as you start to get to know this group, what stands out the most about kind of the foundation that's been laid by Mike and this group uh coming into >> I think it's just the culture. Um like I've said this before, but when I was in Chicago last year, I understood the type of culture that Mike was going to build here. Um and I knew he was going to have success pretty soon. and being here, being kind of back into the fold of the culture, you understand why um the longevity of like obviously being in Tennessee, but being here, why it's a winning culture. Just just basically how guys work. Um guys push through. Um I mean, I don't know if you guys have seen it or whatever, but we run the sleds all the time. You know what I mean? Like that's something that's very unique. It's a very family vibe and um guys just want to work. Guys want to win. Uh it's a very selfish culture and uh something I'm I'm happy and glad to be back a part of. As a former teammate, how excited were you to see the news about AJ Brown coming here? And also, what have you seen out of him in the past, you know, week or so? >> I mean, of course, I was excited. It's something I was, you know, secretly hoping for. Um, but yeah, this same old guy. I mean, I said this before. I mean, he's a phenomenal talent. Uh, haven't seen any any difference from when he was back in Tennessee in his first couple years in the league. And just my 10 game stint uh in Philly, uh, same guy. Same guy to go up and make plays, a one-on-one uh, nightmare for defenses. So, um, obviously it's early right now. It's kind of OTAA stuff like that. So, we're not obviously scheming against him, but a guy that for sure like when I'm back there in the post or I'm back deep, I'm making sure I know exactly where he is because I know that's where, you know, that's where Drake's going with the ball. So, phenomenal guy. Just happy he's, you know, my teammate again. >> Kevin, given your familiarity with Braves, was there anything last year when you were on the outside watching this team that you might see that maybe folks like us or other people wouldn't notice about the team that made it distinct? >> Well, I just think it's just the attention to detail. I will say one thing that I vividly remember being in Tennessee and I know you guys probably have seen it. Um so you know at every single game, you know, win, lose or draw, Mike shakes the head head coach's hand and runs to the tunnel and shakes everybody's hand from players, staff, everybody. Um that let just lets you know how much he cares about this team uh connecting with the guys and uh you know I think guys feel that as well uh the guy that you want to play for. So just little things like that that you know I've you know watched from afar that it's like hey that's the same old Mike that I knew in Tennessee. >> The NFL put out the results of a survey that said 92% of players preferred grass over turf. How would you describe the biggest differences of playing on grass? >> Yeah, I've always been a big proponent of playing on grass. Um, for me, I know that, you know, the statistics doesn't paint the exact picture, but just from being a player who's actually played on turf and on grass, um, you know, it's just a longer recovery process. Um, my joints, espec mainly my ankles, not like knees, but mainly my ankles, uh, joints, uh, take a little bit longer to recover. You know, like on a Wednesday, Tuesday or Wednesday, when you're practicing, you still feel, um, the soreness from that. Um, obviously I've been blessed, highly blessed and favored that I haven't had any any injuries or nothing like that. But I will say just it's more like the recovery time that it takes to recover from grass uh to turf is a lot different. So when you think about playing on a Sunday on turf and then probably a Sunday again, I mean a Thursday game on turf, you know, that it just takes a little bit different recovery. So that's the biggest thing that I see uh in difference- wise. I know the injuries can be a little bit skewed depending on, you know, what survey you're looking at, whatever it may be. But that's the biggest difference that I see. >> Coming from the fields you played at as a home, Tennessee, Philadelphia, Chicago, that factor in how you're going to approach the season? >> Not not a lot honestly because, you know, I'm a very routine based guy anyway. So, I'm I'm going to keep my same routine. I do understand that, you know, I was gonna be playing on turf a lot for my home games, but it truly didn't really make a huge um impact on signing here because like I said, I wanted to play for for Mike. I wanted to play for this for a team like this, a winner. Um so it didn't play a big part, but it is something that's, you know, always conscious on your mind when you know it's a Wednesday practice and it's it's raining. We got to go on the turf. It's like, all right, like might have taken, you know, Tylenol or something like that just to kind of get over the soreness, but uh no, but at least not coming here, it wasn't a a big decision making. Kevin over to your Tennessee days. What's What are the biggest uh differences and the same as you see from Zack Core, you know, given his role, it's much bigger here. >> Yeah, I think that's the biggest difference. I think he's just in a different role. Um, back when I was in Tennessee, Shane Bowen was the defensive coordinator for a lot of those years. So, Zack was kind of more like the defensive assistant, uh, working with the Dline, working with the backer. So, he's just in a more of a vocal role. Um, but you're definitely seeing his uniqueness on kind of how he likes to call the defenses. A little bit different than Shane. I'm not going to obviously going to get into the scheme or nothing like that, but I just think his command of the defense, command of the room, uh his addressing the team is something I'm actually just kind of happy to see because you kind of just see the progression of of a of a younger coach that's obviously running his own room now. >> You're the first to go up against, you know, Drake with AJ and Romeo. What were your first impressions of this offense? Yeah, I mean obviously when uh AJ signed last week he practiced the first day he was here and um I already knew like when he was out there he didn't do a lot of reps but I was like when AJ's out there more than like he's getting the ball and um you can tell they're obviously devel they're already developing that relationship. Um like I said anytime AJ's backside at X I know that's where the ball is probably going. So I try to cheat my alignments and stuff like that. But um like I said man uh Drake is a phenomenal quarterback. I think he's very um just his command of the whole team, you know what I mean? Just even seeing him in the locker room. Uh very approachable guy. Um and then obviously I know AJ, so that relationship has always been there. >> Yeah, it's been pretty cool to see. Um and it's funny because a lot of these guys, whether if it's Dale Pettis or uh even even Skooler, like they're kind of helping me a little bit because obviously I've been a part of this defense, been a part of this team. Um, but at the same time it's some some unique things that we're doing now then versus what we were doing then. So I'm asking all these guys questions. So uh we're all kind of helping each other and obviously I'm giving them tips on you know different ways how to make plays and stuff like that. So it's a collaborative group, a very close group and like I said it's been pretty cool so far. >> How do you approach being a leader among this group where obviously you have a tremendous amount of experience but you're new here. You know this helps you before. So how do you kind of pick your spots when it comes to leading this group? >> I just you know naturally just be myself. I'm not trying to just overly do anything. Um I think especially for a team that was just literally in the Super Bowl. Um you know, I'm coming in bringing obviously be my uniqueness, but at the same time just continue to earn these guys trust and we kind of just discussing different things scheme wise, making sure we're all on the same page and just bringing my, you know, my skill set here to this team. But like said, I'm not trying to overly do anything. I mean, these guys have a great uh leadership group already. I mean, especially in our room uh with Marcus Jones, he's a phenomenal worker. Uh, I've been very impressed with him and just his work ethic and the things he's done. Um, I think he was a captain last year and I can, you know, I I see why. You know what I mean? So, I'm coming in just being myself and, uh, that's really Y absolutely.

title: Zak Kuhr: "Building Off Each Other." | Patriots Press Conference
text: All right. How are we doing? Good. >> How are you >> doing? Good. >> I guess just kind of what has what's it been like for you in this process since the Super Bowl? What's your off season been like putting together what you want to put together as far as what you want from your defense? >> Uh, you know, I wouldn't say it's what I want to do. I always use the word we. It's what we want to do. Again, I don't think there's a lot of difference from last year to this year as far as the staff collaboration. You know, we did that last year and continue to do so. puts a lot of different ideas, not just me. And uh I would say it's pretty smooth going and uh you know, we have a lot of experience with each other and after last year we uh we rift off each other pretty well and we've had some good ideas and uh this is the best time right now to try that stuff out in the lab out there on the field of guys right now. >> Are there any discernable differences between how you want to play how how you want to approach things compared to last year? >> No, I wouldn't say that. I I think, you know, we set standards last year uh philosophically and our play style and it's really just building on that now. We don't want to do any crazy changing or anything like that. Nope. >> Zack, what was your reaction when you got named as the DC officially? >> Uh, you know, I was extremely grateful for that. uh you know like my number one goal doing this is just never to let anybody down and uh to be you know however you want to word it rewarded with that or not. I just felt like you know not goal accomplished but I felt like I did my job to help everybody else out and that that was that was nice to hear. Yeah, >> we talked to Mike about uh Gabe not being here and it feels like there's some guys who maybe uh who were here last year who are taking advantage of some of those opportunities that that really kind of rose because Gabe was here. Braden, uh Elijah, those kind of guys speak to their level of improvement maybe over the course of the offseason, what they've done this spring. >> Yeah, and I wouldn't say what they've done these past few weeks of improving is because of Gabe not being here. I just think whoever is here, they're taking advantage of their their opportunities. Uh Elijah Ponder has been a phenomenal pro this spring. He's taken great steps to improve his technique, uh his play demeanor. Uh Braden Swinson as well, becoming a better pro, uh going about his business better. Uh you know, Draymont's been great. The whole room's been great. Uh, you know, Jesse, Jayloo, he's been great. It's it's a good hardworking room that's taking advantage of all their opportunities. >> The ability that Christian has to take away top targets helps the >> I'm sorry, I can't hear you say it. >> That's right. >> The ability that Christian has take away top targets. >> Yeah. >> How does that help the greater goal of the defense? >> Yeah. I mean, if you got a guy that can take away a guy, it's it's the numbers aren't our advantage now. So, it's absolutely helpful. Uh but really that whole room as a whole and how they play off each other back uh in the safety area and to you know the nickel Marcus CD Gonzo you know KB Craig all those guys that's as a whole unit man that's that's big for us as a defense from the play to an elite level. >> Did you know Christian was going to be back for mini camp? >> Yeah he he's a great communicator. He's been a ultimate pro. Uh he's taken great I mean to even say he's taken strides he he was like that last year. So uh he's the same person and he's doing a great job communicating with us and everything he's be prepared to be out here. >> How's it been working with Shane Bowen again? >> Uh I love working with Shane. Man probably would not be here with uh today without Shane. So we've had always had that chemistry. You know I was grateful that he brought me with him to New York. So we've only had like a year apart now. and uh it's like we were never apart before. >> Yeah, I mean I wouldn't use, you know, filling in a role. Uh he's doing a great job of understanding his strengths and his weaknesses, bettering those weaknesses again, being a better pro day in day out. He has had a lot of improvement. I'm proud of him for that. I was with him in New York, uh you know, two years ago. And to see where he was at then to now is great. And I think it's building his confidence. I'm sure you guys probably know he's a pretty confident person. Uh but he's done a great job of taking steps with his technique, taking the coaching. He's very uh you we talk about uh you know being confident but not complacent, having humility and he's taken that to heart and he takes the coaching. He understands you know what he did wrong. He's told he's done something wrong. He'll ask questions but he's taken big strides with his technique and his game. you mentioned uh having the you know goal not necessarily accomplished by getting that title. How much more maybe even motivate you further to [laughter] >> you know there's two things that really motivate me and I would say it's you know belief and doubt and the people that believe in me I go that much harder for them. Uh obviously, you know, I truly believe that Braves believes in me. Uh Terrell, everybody on the staff, and then truly the people that doubt me drive me that much as well. Uh when I hear that and I hear that, hey, we believe in you. Yes. It's it's it drives me. Absolutely. Uh I wouldn't say to go the extra mile. I feel like I already do that at times, but it it's it's great hearing that people believe in you. >> Zack, you used a lot of personnel last year to come up with the defensive line. Is that something that was a product of what you would like to do? Was it more a product of conditions and the personnel last year? >> This is not just like some type of cliche answer, but really both. Um, you know, you never want to put guys in situations that don't fit them. And when you do have guys that have different uh versatility or different, you know, uh strengths that play off other guys and you want to put them in a package, you know, why not, you know, take advantage of that? And I would say from my offensive background, you know, when you change up personnel quite a bit, it kind it can make the day a little bit harder for the opponent. So having multiplicity with roles with players and packages, if we have the ability to do that, I think it's something we need to take advantage of. [clears throat] >> Sorry, I've already been asked. >> What's Kevin Buyers brought to you defense so far that we >> Yeah, man. Experience, leadership, advice. Uh I've I've sat in the DB room quite a bit this spring during the individual meetings and the great thing about KB is he understands that he's not coming in here and it's like oh you know you're you've been a captain other places and you should be the leader of this room has humility uh earns the respect but then also we'll throw hey you know I've been here for 10 years been this league for 10 years like here's something you should look out for uh I think he's been great with Craig and Craig learning from him. He's he's just a phenomenal person in the room and a f a phenomenal professional that's a great role model you could say someone that's you know everybody that gets in the league wants to be in double digit years in this league and then here's a guy that's doing it right now at a high level even last year in his later years you know so he's just been a great role model uh a great soundboard for those guys. >> Yep. >> What stood out to you about Draymond early on this point? the way he works. Uh, you know, we saw it on film and in the offseason when we looked at the free agents, but he plays with effort and finish, which is our number one, you know, core value here as a team and as a defense. And he just goes about his business. Uh, he wants to get better even though he's a, you know, he's a higher vet. He wants to learn, you know, from Smitty, he wants to learn from Braves, all of us, of, you know, what he can do to do his job better. He takes great pride in his job. be what these three days to be for for you and the defense before they leave and they come back. >> Yeah, just continue to build chemistry, uh improve their technique, improve their fundamentals, and really just, you know, come together as a unit. Uh you know, we're doing some situational stuff today will really help going into uh fall camp. But yeah, just building off each other. >> Back to Draymond. I mean, you got to be excited cuz he's kind of a unique guy. Big enough to put his hand in the dirt, but also fast enough to be outside and rush. I mean, you got to be excited to have a guy. >> Yeah. Anybody that has versatility with uh skill sets and tools and physical tools, we love that. Anytime we can have different chess pieces. Absolutely. Yep. >> How'd you see some of the younger quarterbacks take advantage of their opportunities when Christian and Carlton? Yeah, I I'm extremely excited about that room's competition. I mean, there's, you know, four or five guys that are all competing for those spots and those reps. And I think it's, you know, the iron sharpens iron where they all see an opportunity. They're all taking advantage of it and they all want to, you know, capitalize on it. And I think they're all pushing each other. That's going to be a fun competition to watch for sure. >> Yep. Appreciate it, guys. Thank you.

title: Mike Vrabel: "We've Seen Growth in a Lot of Players." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Go ahead, Ken. >> Um, during the stretch of the offse program and the workouts, have you already seen some growth in Drake May? And if so, how so? >> Um, yeah. I mean, I think we've seen growth in in a lot of players and especially um some of the younger ones, which I would consider Drake, you know, going into his third year, one of the those younger players. And I think that Josh and and Ashton have given him uh some really, you know, positive things to work on, some great areas of focus and, you know, being able to um you know, try to try to limit mistakes at the line of scrimmage, right? get us in the best play. And and not that, you know, we're going to be perfect, but being able to to use every resource that we have to to get us uh in into the right play and be able to um give us an option to to have a positive play. And, you know, whether they're pressuring or they're in a look that, you know, isn't advantageous to the play. And you know, we don't want to be tentative, you know, so there's a fine line of that, but I think expanding some of that into the the second year of the system uh has been good to see here uh in the spring. >> Like anything report wise share or attendance or anything like that? Is everybody here that you need here? >> Uh everybody under contract is here and and accounted for. So, uh, as it relates to practice, you know, everybody will have different plan at practice and, you know, some guys will some be full, some guys will be limited, you know, some guys will work on the lower field, but, you know, it's been a good day and it's much better than yesterday when when they weren't here. And it's been a great day to have everybody back and, you know, coach and teach and and moving into the red zone, which is uh which is so critical, which is somewhere where, you know, we struggled defensively, except for the playoffs, um, which I think the big reason of of why we were able to get to where we got to offensively, just too many negative plays and and turnovers. So, um, did a lot of good things offensively, just pretty pretty average in the red zone. >> Gabe has signed. Is he part of that group that's here? >> He's not part of that group that's here. So, >> at all, >> great question. Go ahead. >> Um, do you attribute his absence to last year we saw a rise in second round picks hold out until they signed their contract? Do you attribute it to that or >> I don't attribute to anything other than, you know, he's not here and that um he's not under contract at at this current time. So I don't I don't want to say that there's a reason for it other than that that's what it is right now. >> I know he's on the practice. >> Is he dealing with anything physical? >> Again, he had a procedure and he's not under contract. >> I know he's on the practice field this spring. How much, if at all, have you had a chance to kind of work with him a little bit >> with Gabe? Yeah, >> not at all. We've talked and communicated and met him numerous times before the the draft process, but um not not on the grass. >> Has that been frustrating for you that you haven't been able to >> It hasn't not one bit. Been excited to to work with the the players here and um have have learned that there's only so many things that you can control and uh excited about the development of the guys uh in that room. ones that have been here that you know are going into their second year or the ones that we drafted or the ones that we signed in the postdraft or the ones uh that we signed in free agency. >> March how far behind will be by this? >> I I don't you know I mean I don't know you know what I mean? So I I know that we were here for 8 weeks and 10 11 OTAAS or whatever that is. I don't you know I mean I don't know can't can't say won't say I don't think that's fair to anybody. Harold Landry was still doing some rehab. Where where's he at physically at this point? >> Uh, again, Harold's played a lot of football and uh and so we just have to try to, you know, this is all part of everyone has a little different plan. I think you guys understand that having spent a year with us and kind of how we operate. Um, so he's very involved, very heavily involved in the meetings and the workouts and and in a leadership role. And for for him to take reps right now in the spring, I I feel like is is unnecessary. And, you know, we'll just keep working to to make sure that he's ready to go when when we need him. >> You referenced some of the younger guys who were who have been here. very specifically about Braden and Elijah, how they've done with the maybe the added opportunities they've gotten over the course of >> Well, I think physically they they've both have worked really hard with Frank and his um group um and the time that they spent away from here, however long that was. Uh that was uh evident when they came back. I just think from a maturity, you know, from getting stronger and being, you know, better conditioned and those things really stood out and I think that through the course of the, you know, eight or nine weeks that that's that's become evident on the field as well. >> Conversations with guys who do you have conversations with guys who were not at OTAAS or do you just move on at this point? Do you talk about why they were not here? Do I have conversations with guys that aren't here or >> Sorry, let me clarify. Yep. >> So, guys who missed OTAAS, do you speak to them about why they missed OTAAS or do you just move on at this point now that you're in mini camp? >> No, those are voluntary. I mean, I I mean, I talk to most of the players all the time. There's communication, you know, whether they're here or or they're not. Um, you know, so again, there's multiple reasons on on our team and across the league of why guys wouldn't be at a a voluntary workout and uh just coach them when they get here. That's usually the best plan of attack to have Christian Gonzalez back and just how conversations gone with him as he tries to negotiate for a new extension. >> Good conversations have been great and talked to him about his event last week. um talk to him about normal things that we talk about and then you know but it's good to have everybody back in here that uh that either was here last week or that wasn't. It's just good to have a you know almost a complete football team here and uh excited to keep working. So, go ahead. >> Tackle. Um, you had Kyus Tonga kind of >> be so much louder with these vultures over here. >> I'm trying. >> Go ahead. >> When it comes to nose tackle, you had Kyus Tonga in that room last year. Um, Cory Duran, we spoke with him last week and he kind of said he anticipates filling that role and moving into that spot. What have you seen from him this offseason? Is that a role you anticipate him kind of filling? >> Well, I don't want to fill any role right now. I think that uh that will be an opportunity for Cory. Um and by saying that, I'm excited for Cory. I'm excited to that we had a full off seasonason with him, that we'll have a full training camp with him. He came in and quickly uh earned the confidence of the coaching staff and and his teammates and and had a great play demeanor and so I'm happy for his ability to be able to help us last year. Um but but again, that has to all be um played out. um you know, in training camp and there's other young guys and you know, Lenny Lenny T and Josh Farmer and and Gregory and and everybody else that that those are all it's a it's a good group. Um and I'm excited and I know the the defensive coaches are excited about working with those guys, too. So, you know, have just having him in the system another year and being able to coach him in the offseason and coach him at training camp hopefully will will only help. But he he did a lot of good things for us last year. >> Mike, did you one more thing on that? Did you know that he was going to need a procedure when you drafted him? >> Again, he just had to have a procedure and he's not under contract. So, you know, we're excited about the Gabe, the person that he is, the play style, the his production in college, and you know, all that. And so, when that gets resolved, you know, we'll have him in here and we'll coach him and uh I'm sure we'll find a way for him to help our football team. >> You understand with negotiations with Gonzalez at this moment? I don't I'm not involved with the negotiations. I'm involved with coaching this team. >> No update. Nothing like that. >> Nothing to I mean he's still under his you know what I mean? I don't think there's anything you know to report. I'll say that. >> Kan Booty right now. >> How or what >> things with Kan Booty? Uh has he been expecting to participate fully here? And >> I don't know if he'll participate fully just because I don't think that's fair to to him to just say, "Hey, you know, go go run, you know, 20 reps." Again, I think the part of this is about evaluating where guys are, getting them um, you know, reaclimated to what the new stuff is that we're putting in in the red zone. Um, and then based on on how he does and and looks, I think that that could that could certainly change. But, you know, again, we we want to be smart with with everybody that we have. And you know, for the guys that we haven't seen, I I think it's only right to, you know, make sure that they're, you know, where everybody else is based on how we practice. >> Are you also expecting Christian to be limited for the same reason? >> Yeah, I would say just like everybody else, everybody has a plan and I got to make sure everybody's working and uh and getting what they need to get. >> Mike, now that AJ's been here for a week, how's everything going? >> I think uh good. But I think the weekend probably served him well to be able to take a deep breath and and get some rest. I'm sure sure it was a, you know, been a whirlwind for him, but you know, he's excited about learning the system and, you know, eventually, you know, moving around and doing different things and, you know, but I, you know, I think it's it's been great. Um, just having him around and and, you know, just continuing to to integrate himself into our football team. Mike, you mentioned at the combine asking the coaches to come up bring some new ideas when you guys reconvened. Um, what have those tried to achieve or unlock defensively and are you pleased with the progress there? >> Uh, you mean from the defensive side of the ball? I mean, I think you're always just looking, you know, spring is a time where the touchdown the touchdowns don't count and and the sacks don't count and so, you know, I think you try to, you know, figure out different blitzes and disguises and and, you know, I appreciate what everybody brought to the table and the ideas that they had and all all the phases of first and second down and, you know, the things that we try to add on third down and then really try to shore up the the red zone. So the spring is the time where you evaluate the stuff that you try to come up with and you know what it may look like or what the issues are and then uh as you get closer to training camp some of that may get paired down. >> Mentioned uh you mentioned red zone efficiency in terms of the personnel that you brought in in the offseason both on the offensive or the defensive side of the ball. How much of a focus was how how good they are in in the red zone in terms of bringing guys in? >> Well, it's a critical area. You know, it's a critical situation. you know, we were, you know, fifth in red zone drives offensively, but unfortunately, we're middle of the pack and, you know, too many negative plays, too many too many turnovers. Almost half of our turnovers were in the red zone. So, that that that hurt you there. uh you know and then defensively just you know you have to be on body, you have to be tight coverage, making sure teams don't run the football in on you and just understanding how uh critical every yard is and being great tacklers and um communicating all the the motions and the pre-step motions and and different routes that combinations that they have. like on the bigger scale, what are you looking for of your team uh you know that you can rely on that can tell you the foundation you built last year is solid enough and not really rebuild? >> Well, I mean I think that that's probably not going to I don't know if that happens during the spring. I think we can still focus on on the things that we think are important for our identity and and and how we want to win football games and and how we want to prepare. Um but re really a lot of that comes in training camp and being able to to call yourself um through through some of the rigors of the season. So as we continue to build that foundation and how we work and how we practice uh against each other uh is going to be something that's critical and that's how you improve uh in training camp that you know some of those battles that you have in training camp give you a lot of confidence um you know going into the season. I know running back tough position to evaluate this time of the year. But what have you seen from Lan Larrison and how he's grown from last year, especially overcoming? >> Well, worked really hard and just to to you work through the injury and work through uh and just continue to to get stronger and give himself another opportunity uh going into training camp. So, mentally um he's not a rookie. I think just the experience probably may seem somewhat new to him again u when we get to training camp but um you know as a player that's trying to find a role on special teams and and and you're right it is hard to to you know half the battle for the backs is being identify where the pressure is coming from what their blitz pickup is and then there's really not much of a blitz pickup everybody kind of stops once they get there. So, uh, he's done a good job with that. You know, a lot of that will come with the pads and whether they can, you know, break tackles and and and pick up pressure. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Lane Johnson and More on New Offense and Offseason
text: I mean, what were your uh what was your initial reaction to the whole Stoutland thing? And >> yeah, I mean, it was it was a um you know, it was a shocking ordeal for me, but you know, after being in the league all these years, um you know, you can kind of see when things um you know, aren't going the way that we want to, but um you know, it's uh for me it's just I'm trying to learn a new offense and uh do the best I can with that. Um, but yeah, I mean, far as replacing Stout, it's going to be hard to, you know, replace that kind of guy in my life being the mentor and just, uh, you know, my coach all these years, but, um, you know, with how our system is now, there's a lot to learn. I really like Coach Cooper a lot. Um, and so I think, you know, hopefully our offense won't be as stagnant as what it was last year. We'll be able to evolve some. >> What's it like after 13 seasons to have a new O line coach? >> I mean, I'm about it. Um, you know, um, Coach Cooper played for lots of years in the league. So, um, not only coming to me as a coach, but as a player. Got a lot of respect for him. Super smart. And I just think how this offense here will will help us. Um, you know, I think we're just, uh, stretching the field, uh, stretching the defense more. Um, you know, I think it'll help us with our, uh, run blocking angles. I think it'll help us some in pass pro. Um, yes. So, I've never had like any guard help all these years. Like, it's always been one-on-one. So, having the ability if I get beat inside, having a guard come out and help me is a big deal for me. So, I'm I'm like you. Very excited. So, um, that's pretty cool. >> How are you approaching? Do you work more with the guards and conversation then? >> Yeah, I mean, right now we're just uh, you know, a lot of this, you know, football is um, very similar things are going on, but just different terminology. So, just getting the new wording, um, working the new cad, you know, working our cadence more. So, being more disciplined with that. But, um, you know, I think with this offense, we'll be able, like I said, we'll be able to stretch stretch and and really work, um, you know, our zone game and and get the defense running and and work things off of that. So, um, you know, I'm really excited what it can do, um, you know, just for tackles. I think it'll it'll open up a lot in our game. >> What was your decision making process in terms of deciding to come back? Yeah, I was just, man, I thought I was having a really good season last year and uh man, there was nobody more disappointed than me uh not being able to come in and play um to finish it out. So, I just I didn't want to go out that way. Uh you know, I think um far as performance-wise, I felt like I was still performing the same same as I always have. Just I had this foot injury. It was, you know, I've been able to play through stuff uh throughout the years, but this was just something that it took time and so and that's something that I didn't have at that at that point in the season. So, you know, it was uh um probably around February, March where I started feeling 100%. But it, you know, it took some time for it to for it to heal up, but yeah, I I just I didn't want to go out on that note last year. >> Before it felt 100%, did you consider retirement? Was there a point where you didn't actually know you were going to come back? >> No, I mean, I I wanted to play. I mean, only thing that's keep me um you know, thinking about retiring is just family. You know, mom and dad getting older. uh you know, you miss a lot of time, but other than that, man, I I love this game so much. I love competing with all my teammates. I love I love uh just, you know, becoming an older player. Um a lot of guys trend down in their 30s. I feel like my my career has been the opposite where my career started to blossom in my 30s. So, um you know, last year me being out of the game was kind of, hey, um you know, if you don't stay healthy, it's going to be a glimpse of what it could become. But but like I said, I wanted to come back and finish on a strong note and and uh and really say, you know, I got everything out of myself. And >> with the Liz Frank injury, they never put you on IR, but you end up being out for the rest of the season. What What happened there? >> I think I mean, I was trying to come back. I mean, I was I was rehabbing. I was I was practicing and so like towards the um you know, the playoff game, I went out there to practice and uh after a couple series, my foot would just swell up and then the mobility piece, it became to where it was just I couldn't function. So, um, you know, it wasn't because of trying. Um, and so that's really what that was about. >> Lane, um, Chris Chris Cooper was mentioning the other day how important it is for guys like you and, you know, who've been around a while to have that buy in, I guess, with what he's teaching and everything. >> What is it about him that kind of convinced you, you know, that you will buy in or are you buying in? >> Yeah. Um, just explain experience and then, you know, I got to talk to a lot of the Minnesota guys. Uh Brian O'Neal, who I respect a lot, um you know, said that was their favorite line, his favorite O line coach he's had since he's been in the NFL. So coming from a guy like that, it didn't take me long to realize what kind of teacher he was uh in the classroom. Um even some of the remote stuff I'm doing on Zoom, just a great teacher. So he knows how to really apply just from being as a player. The communication aspect I think is really good. But um just this new system I think is um way he stress is just going to be more efficient for us. I think our our run blocking angles will be more conducive. We'll be able to be in three-point stance a little bit more. Kind of what we did with Doug. If we had a tight end with us, we'd be in three-point detach not. But um you know, I think that helps us with some of our landmarks. >> How's the health right now? And it's it seemed in your career like foot and the ankle stuff is what bothers you the most. How do you keep it fresh? Yeah, I mean I felt I mean other than last year I had a stinger, but other than that I felt like I was uh fine, but it really was the first play in Detroit last year. I went to power step and tried to anchor and I felt my foot pop. I thought it was like planter fascia on my foot and then after like the next series I took a bull rush from uh Aiden Hudson. I couldn't anchor and I was like, "Okay, something's wrong." But yeah, it was just it was really um yeah, it was a blow to me. I mean, I was I was having a great year. I feel like I was in a point in the season where we were starting to make a turn, have ability to to do more, but uh when it came down to this, man, it was just it's one of those things. It just took so much time. It took a lot of rehab. But um yeah, even like February, March, that's when I started feeling 100%. Uh you know, I talked to Zach um Bond, he had the a similar injury in college to Kobe, you know, coming back from this injury. There'll be some soreness, but uh that's to be expected, but yeah, man, I feel good. Uh but it just it took a long time to get here. Um, I wish I could have done this, you know, at the end of last year. >> Wayne, we have Dallas coming down. >> What do you think of Markeel? >> You said that the offense, you hope that the offense won't be as stagnant as it was last year. What do you see now both on the field and in the classroom that gives you the confidence that >> Yeah, it's just different uh points of emphasis. I think uh run game is, >> you know, you have the ability to stretch it front side, but also the running back has the ability to read backside blocks more than maybe what we did in previous years. So, um I just think it's uh for us it really does a good job of allowing us to run. We have a lot of athletic guys up front. So, being able to stretch the field, uh make the detackles run, make the linebackers run, cover all this ground, and then I think setting up with a play action is just going to be u it's going to be a whole lot tougher to to distinguish what we're doing. Whole lot harder to catch on tails um with stuff that we're doing. So I think this stuff is a lot easily uh you know we can disguise it more and uh yeah just I've watched this system Kubak Shanahan style of offense you know from afar and I've always envied wanting to you know be a part of it so here I am after all these years getting a chance not to say that we're going to be better but you know there's a lot to learn but I think we have the ability to be more than what we were last year um be a lot more than what we were in the run game and I think that's going to open up the pass game too. What's been your first impressions? First impressions of Shawn Manion. Um the way he changed >> uh man, super smart guy. So he played with Isaac in college at Oregon State. So obviously asked Isaac about him, but um you know him being here at this age, uh you're not going to be here without a you know, brilliant offensive mind. Um but he's just he's very good with players, very personable and uh yeah, I mean we see um you know what his what his vision is and we're still picking up you know learning you know stuff through film and you know um way Green Bay did it when he's in Green Bay. But he's very good, very assertive. Uh very big on communication. So uh you know we're just getting started. We'll turn it up more in training camp. But yeah, I'm just really really excited what we could be and what this offense could be. You said you watched the system for a long time, interviewed it from afar. How many questions have you built up about it and how many of those have been answered so far? >> Yeah. Uh, one of is just having, you know, you have the ability for a guard to leave and come and tee off a DN when he's making a move inside. But, uh, really, you know, we have a lot of athletic guys up front that can really run and stretch the field. So, I think for us, it's really getting aiming points and getting to them fast. And it's so much, you know, it's attacking and it's really making the, you know, the the defenders run. It's making linebackers cover a lot of ground. Um, and so for us, I think when you do that, you'll be able to tire out the defense and then you'll get to where you can run more of a a power style later in the games. But, you know, I really just I've watched how they've attacked offenses throughout the years. really stretch the field, get them going and then um tee off on them whenever um you know a point of the game comes into into perspective. But yeah, it just I think it allows the guys to play more loose, play more free, get some free free shots with the guards, you know, myself included. So, um, yeah, the ability to be more physical, um, you know, in in some certain instances. >> How about practice skills? Having been with Stout as long as you were, you know, you knew what to expect every practice in terms of like individual. Has it been weird? >> Yeah, it was totally different. So, uh, you know, I think I think a lot of a good is going to come of it. So, new drills, new tempo. So, yeah, it was it was a little bit used. Uh, it's my second or third practice. So yeah, it was a little bit it was it was a game changer me coming out there and getting used to that not having Stout out there. So yeah, it's it's it's been a it's been a different um you know year, but I've had time to process. I've had time to talk with Stout um obviously with all the new guys in. So yeah, um you know, change is what the NFL is all about and uh yeah, I'm just I'm just embracing it as I go and uh thankful that that I'm here, man. 36. So, it feels weird to say that I'm that age, but uh yeah, I'm I'm hoping this will be a great year for us, a great year for me, and we can write a lot of the wrongs that, you know, we had >> All right, thanks everybody. Dallas, let's come down. >> Dallas, another offseason where there's like little uncertainty about whether you'd be back or not. You know, what made you decide to to return? >> Um, you know, it just kind of came down to a good opportunity, you know, being able to play here for eight years. Um, we've put a lot of good runs together. Uh, been able to do special things and, um, I feel like playing in an organization like the Eagles is special and I think we can do uh, special things this year and uh, you know, I didn't want to leave and not be part of it. So, um, you know, ultimately I chose to uh, come back and hopefully uh, put another great year together. >> Just adding to that, Dallas, you've been here for a while. Your name is slowly rising on some of the alltime stats list. just how special has it been for you to only play for one team and build roots here and uh be so accomplished as an Eagle? >> Yeah. Uh obviously it's really cool. You look at uh some of the other Eagles legends I've been a part of. You know, uh Kelsey Fletch uh BG Lane. Uh they're so so beloved here. Uh played an entire career. Um you know, I think all of them went through a little adversity here or there um throughout their playing career. Um and that's just part of it. But, uh, no, it's it's cool, um, to be able to play for one team as long as I have, uh, you build so many special connections around the bu building, around the facility, um, around the city. So, uh, just being able to be in one spot, uh, is pretty cool. >> What makes you excited to play in this new offensive system on a minute and what not changes or differences have you noticed so far? >> Yeah, obviously, um, there's similarities. Uh, you can only do so much on offense. Um, but a lot of the key emphasises are a little bit different. Um, I feel like through watching, uh, what he he wants to happen. Uh, there's a lot of easy touches to the tight ends, uh, getting the ball in space. Um, scheming ways to get us open. Um, so I'm excited for that. Um, I think, uh, the tight end's kind of a backbone of the offense both in the run game, play action, pass game. So, um, I think it'll be a really good system to be able to play in. Have you spent much time talking to or or studying tight ends that have excelled in the system? >> Yeah, obviously uh you watch uh George KD a lot. Um watched uh Tucker Craft, uh some of the other tight ends that have been um with the Packers over the last couple years. Um see a lot of those clips and see what they did well and um how they were able to attack the run game. Uh use that in the play action, get the ball in space and what they're able to do with it. But, um, a lot of the tight ends in this system, uh, find ways to get get the ball quite a bit and, uh, find find open space. >> As someone who's, uh, who's who's been that second round rookie before, what's your plan or or I to I guess navigate the relationship with Eli Sal? >> Yeah, I'm I'm here for whatever he needs. Um, obviously, anytime you can bring more competition into the room, it just elevates everybody. Um, so I'm excited to compete, work with him all the time. Um, but yeah, really whatever he needs, I'm here. uh that he can lean on me and you know I'm excited to push him. Um obviously going way back uh we've had a good flow of tight ends and you know hopefully I can help him carry that legacy ultimately. >> You were very close to Jason. How was that transition and your first impressions of Ryan taking over the room? >> Yeah, obviously uh losing Jason was tough. You know uh had a lot of love with him was for five years. Um I feel like he really helped me grow as a player, grow as a person. Uh, so hearing that news, uh, it was tough. Um, but it it's part of the business. Um, he knows that, I know that. Um, so, you know, you just you come in here with an open mind and, uh, get to know a guy and, uh, figure him out personally. Let him figure you out. But, uh, you know, me and Ryan have a good relationship. It continues to grow each and every day. And, um, you know, you get new coaching points, you get new, uh, perspective of the game. So, um, I'm excited to learn from him and work work with him. You >> mentioned that the tight end position is kind of central to this offense. Uh, you mentioned that the tight end position is kind of central to this offense. Uh, how so in terms of like the blocking? >> Yeah. Um, you know, it kind of starts uh Lane kind of mentioned it, the point of attack. Um, you know, possibly being on the front side of runs a little bit more. um starting the you know where the running back's going to read. He's going to start out there and uh work his way back. But um yeah, I think uh you you got to be able to block in this offense and uh you know, we've been working on it quite a bit, but um I feel like it'll go as far as uh we can take it. >> Did you know Johnny Munt at all before and the resources he'd been as you guys made this switch to the new offense? >> Um I knew of him. Uh, I know a lot of people that he played with, Brian O'Neal when he was with the Vikings, uh, talks very highly of him. Watch his film. Um, you know, another I think he's going into year 10, so another vet like that. Uh, we can pick each other's brains. Uh, talk about little differences that we do in our in our game. But, uh, I've really enjoyed having Johnny there. Uh, he's a fun guy to be around. And, uh, like I said earlier, you know, the more uh, good tight ends we get in the room, the better it's going to make all of us. >> Easy touch. You talked about the easy touches in this offense with the tight end and you've worked with Jaylen Herz a lot of offenses. What's what's kind of been the conversation between you two and how you guys approach this this year this those easy touches? >> Yeah, it's kind of the same, you know. Uh I always want to be a very friendly guy to the quarterback. Uh get open when he needs somebody. Um so it's just kind of the same thing. Both of us are learning the new offense, trying to uh get the little things dialed down. But I feel like he's been doing a great job picking it up. um when the play actions come, he he's great at that. Being able to evade, create space for himself and find find me when I'm open. So, uh it's just kind of dialing in the little details of timing, uh what he sees when, uh you know, you have an option to go one way or the other. So, uh just finding the little details. >> If I can take you back to that first week of the league year, did you get a sense of of what the market would be elsewhere? And like was it the opportunity here? Was it the you you mentioned opportunity, but like was it uh the the loyalty you had to the Eagles or was it the offense? What was it in in in particular? >> Yeah, it's it's a little bit of everything, you know. Uh I was able to test free agency a little bit. Uh you know, had opportunities to go elsewhere. Um nothing was a better opportunity than I thought I could have here. Um you know, being able to play in the same place for 9 years is special. um it would have had to be something really drastic to um have me try to sign somewhere else. >> Going back to Eli, where has he uh specifically stood out to you in getting to know him and seeing him practice? >> Yeah. Um you know, he's he's been a good rookie. He's uh put his head down and worked. Probably the thing you noticed the most about him uh is in the weight room when we do the force play jumps. He he can jump out of the gym. He's super explosive in that aspect. and uh you know just continuing to build on uh what he knows at this position. Obviously hasn't played it his whole life, so he's still kind of new to the transition. So uh just trying to help him with the little details that I've learned over my career and uh try to advance him as fast as we can. Some >> of the legends that have come through here to see Lane in year 14 still doing this level. Is that um does that serve as sort of a a benchmark for you? Uh, you know, Lane Lane's special. Uh, obviously 14 years is incredible at that position. You know, uh, he doesn't look any different than when I first got here. You know, he looks just as explosive. Um, you know, the way he goes to work every day, he he's a dominant force on the field. And, uh, yeah, anytime you can play that long at a high level, uh, I think it's an inspiration to all of us to be able to keep going. Obviously, he's uh handled his adversity just like everybody else in this league. Battled through injuries and things, but uh yeah, I don't know if I'll make 14 years like he did, but uh it's special to see, special to be a part of. >> Thanks, Alex. >> Good afternoon. >> What's up, >> what are just your early impressions of the city, this franchise, and how they do things around here? >> Um shoot, with my short time being here from the city, they do got a lot of good food. I feel I done tried a lot of cheese steak, a lot of pizza, and uh from the team and organization, you can just tell it's a lot of history, a lot of winning, a lot of competing, and just being here with these guys. It's honestly been a lot of fun. You know, I've been working real hard, and it's not a shortness for greatness throughout this building. >> Big fan, you know, said we watched you film, were you surprised that you weren't getting lucrative long deals? You know, when you entered the process, were you surprised? and what did it lead to the um you know coming here? >> Uh yeah, I was a little surprised. God plan was to put me here with a great team and give me another chance to, you know, win a Super Bowl and be successful here. Now that you've played in the system a little bit, a little bit, what do you like about what uh Vic, you know, allows us quarterbacks to do? >> Oh, shoot. He just puts us in the right places and he lets us play to our strengths and just being in his defense, you you're going to grow a lot, you know, especially uh working off technique is one of my things in my game cuz I know I'm a press corner, but also, you know, I got to play off technique sometimes, too. and being able to come here and, you know, work on that technique throughout this training and being able to understand the defense and learn different ways to play my techniques in this defense. That's something I've been trying to do, uh, as as we go each day. >> What What are your impressions of Quinn Yan so far? >> Um, real real great player. I mean, even when I signed here, uh, I had spoke highly of him and it's still the same way, man. A great player. U, very smart, even better person. you know, he's going to be an amazing father. He just had a kid, so you know, u I'm his brother, man. So, me being here, uh, it's nice to team up and, you know, just feed off each other. >> What have your battles with Devonte been like? And what do you what's covering them like? >> Uh, it's pretty cool, honestly, just because when you come from a team with great receivers, you go to another team with great receivers. And whenever you got great receivers, you're going to make great corners. So going against him, going against Wigs, the whole receiving crew has been pretty cool, honestly. Uh just because uh I'm seeing new looks and I'm going against great receivers who are very respected in this league. >> How do you think you played this this spring? >> How do you think you play? >> Uh I feel like I've been doing pretty well. You know, I'm still picking up on new things. I still got to, you know, get more into the playbook, you know, certain plays. Uh you know, just got to, you know, learn and buy into it even more. But I feel like I've been doing well. Um, I feel like my teammates, they, you know, trust me a little bit and, uh, I just got to keep building off from the work I've been putting in. >> What do you think the potential is of this secondary? I mean, on paper, it looks uh, it looks quite high. >> Uh, honestly, just, uh, I feel like we can be one of the best, you know, secondary groups in the league, and we we all are confident about that, and these guys have showed that with their work. I showed it with the work I put in. So, being able to to join them, you know, the sky is the limit and I feel like we can be one of the best groups in the NFL. >> Last year, uh, personal flags were a part of your year. How have you addressed that going forward? >> Just celebrating with my team. Um, you know, it's crazy cuz that's the most taunting penalties I ever got. If you look at any other years, I never got taunting penalties. Well, I won the year before, but other than that, I really wasn't getting toning penalties, but I mean, whenever you make plays, you got to celebrate. And I just got to be smarter when I celebrate. And I'm with another team that has a lot of players on here who are very passionate about their game, just like I'm passionate. So, we'll be able to celebrate together. >> I feel like every time we talk about you with somebody else, they talk about your length, and you don't see 6'4 cornerbacks every day. Why? Why does it work for you, do you think? >> Uh, shoot. I've been just blessed with, you know, amazing gifts. I've play I ran track my whole life. I played basketball, played baseball, and and all transitions to the football world. So, uh, you know, I I've been blessed with the the height, the length, and speed, and it's pretty cool to, you know, be recognized by that. But at the same time, me being different from the other corners, you know, body and the athletic type, you know, I still got to go out there and produce and do the right things and use my gifts the right way. >> Was there a learning process for you to kind of figure out how to use that as an advantage out there on the field? >> Uh, a little bit. I mean, I was a wide receiver first before I was a corner. Like, I played 15 games a corner, 16 games a corner in college. So, I was still learning year three and four how to use my length and I feel like that's what make me a great player. You know, you can still be going along in your career and you still willing to learn new things and add it to your game. So, that's something I've been trying to do. >> Couple more. We got J. >> Are there anything like difficult in terms of coaches coaching you because you're you're such an unusual body type? >> Uh, a little bit. Uh just talking to the coaches is pretty interesting cuz uh you know they haven't like coached a tall corner and I haven't had these coaches before cuz obviously I'm the new guy. So it's both a new learning curve for both of us but at the same time you know it's great to you know be able to have a coach that never had a player like me just because we can learn different ways from each other. Rick, when you uh arrived, the team posted a social video and one of the first things you asked is, "Where's the guy from Invincible?" >> You a fan of that movie? >> Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. So, that was probably one of the early Disney movies, especially cuz I liked football movies. I used to watch all the football movies from any given Sunday, The Comebacks, uh Varsity Blues, uh Friday Night Lights. You I'm from Texas, so Friday Night Lights is what we like to watch. So, uh Invincible was a pretty cool movie. Just watching it on Disney Channel. I just like the story of him just being a guy being able to to get off the street and come and play football with everybody else cuz it's a lot of guys out there on the street that wish they can have the chance just like us and we got these chances every day and we live this life but for a random person to you know get a chance to show what he wanted to do and showcase his skill. I just thought it was a pretty cool movie. >> All right, thanks everybody is coming down. Jix, how's uh Jonathan Bernard fit in and and what has his uh UNK uh aspect meant to uh your group? >> That's my dog. How you know we call him, man? >> Told us >> for real. Uh it's just always cool. Like I said, my rookie year, uh, I just am always eager to learn new information and to have somebody who's been successful in the league for a long time and is so confident in his style because he's he's uh put a lot of work into his moves and he's very confident in it to learn a little bit of just about his his process and his approach to the game has been uh invaluable information. So, it's like uh just Yeah. No, I love having him in the room. Real cool dude. He he fits right in. able to joke around with him and everything like he's been here forever. >> Have you been able to take much stock of your own journey yet at this point? I know it's only been a couple years. Third round pick, position change. You you're on a pretty good trajectory right now. And what's next for you? >> Uh man, just keep working head down. Uh, I definitely do look back and you know how on different apps you get the the year ago and so I I get I get those type of things and I'm able to look at those and and it's really cool to see and it's it makes me smile because I I have come a long way and it's just it makes me more excited to work. So, you know, going into my next year putting my head down, I I know I've I've learned some more from from last season just playing. I've learned more just watching a whole bunch more film, being around a whole bunch more people, knowing what questions to ask. So, I'm excited to put that into effect and I just want to keep on on a upward trajectory. >> How do you feel last season went for you personally? And do you feel like that can be something that props you forward this year, the plays you made, moments? >> Uh, it was definitely uh it definitely gave me some more confidence that I'm going in the right direction. So that was very um motivating and uh exciting to see and go going into next year, you know, like I was just saying, it's just more work. title: Giants Minicamp Day One Recap | Big Blue Kickoff Live | New York Giants
text: Ah, yes. A good Tuesday afternoon to one and all. Welcome to today's episode of Big Blue Kickoff Live presented by Cadillac, the official luxury vehicle of the New York Football Giants. Uh, and it was good to see both obviously looking in good health. Uh, and both making their presence felt here at the Giants practice facility. >> Yeah, I mean, look, it's always nice to have some of the greats come back, you know, whether it's to watch practice, just to come say hi to the team and go to a team meeting, whatever it might be. Yeah, no question about it. And obviously the the Giants, those are two legendary linebackers when you're looking at LT and Harry Carson and Lawrence Taylor, I don't even think it's much of an argument. The greatest defensive player that the National Football League has ever seen. So the knowledge that this team can be able to grab from them and I love the fact that they were breaking down the team after the game after practice yesterday and after the mandatory mini camp, that is fantastic. you could pull a lot. And then when you look at, you know, the excitement around this linebacking core um for the New York Giants, um you know, I had an opportunity to chat with Charlie Bolan last week and a nice conversation and talking about Kavon Tibido and obviously talking about um you know, Arll Reese and talking about Tmaine Edmonds and everything that comes along with it. First and foremost, the big physical linebacker that Tummaine Edmonds is coming over from the Chicago Bears and then Arll Reese, the tackling machine, and the speed unquestioned coming from Ohio State. >> Yeah, I mean, I've spoken about this many times since since Arl Reese was drafted because, you know, when Tmaine Edmunds was signed, obviously, when was it? Three months ago. Almost three months. Wow. Three months ago. >> Time goes by fast. Yeah. Uh, you know, we spoke about, you know, for the first or the next five, sixish weeks, we said, "All right, well, the Giants now have one really tall, lengthy, fast linebacker." And then at the time, Micah McFaten was, you know, the projected starter next to him because that was, you know, the next guy up. Obviously, that changed with the selection of Arval Reese. All of a sudden, that gave the Giants two incredibly big, long, athletic linebackers. Uh Brian Burns was asked about the two of them together yesterday and he started off by saying you look at them they look like one of you know they look like one of us in terms of an edge rusher cuz that's how big and tall and just built that these guys are. No doubt in the National Football League. But, um, you know, I like that description uh from Brendan Brown. I I do. title: What is Kayshon Boutte's future with the New England Patriots? | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: Oh, that was some good pick up, man.
